<h1 id="email-activity-beta">Email Activity (beta) v1.0.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

The Beta endpoints for the new Email Activity APIs - functionality is subject to change without notice. You may not have access to this Beta endpoint.

Email Activity offers filtering and search by event type for two days worth of data. There is an optional add-on to store 60 days worth of data. This add-on also gives you access to the ability to download a CSV of the 60 days worth of email event data. The Beta endpoints for the new Email Activity APIs - functionality is subject to change without notice. You may not have access to this Beta endpoint.

Email Activity offers filtering and search by event type for two days worth of data. There is an optional add-on to store 60 days worth of data. This add-on also gives you access to the ability to download a CSV of the 60 days worth of email event data.

* <a href="http://api.sendgrid.com/v3">http://api.sendgrid.com/v3</a>

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-ip-access-management">IP Access Management</h1>

## Retrieve all recent access attempts

<a id="opIdGET_access_settings-activity"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/access_settings/activity \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /access_settings/activity`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of all of the IP addresses that recently attempted to access your account either through the User Interface or the API.**

<h3 id="retrieve-all-recent-access-attempts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of IPs to return.|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": [
    {
      "allowed": false,
      "auth_method": "Web",
      "first_at": 1444087966,
      "ip": "1.1.1.1",
      "last_at": 1444406672,
      "location": "Australia"
    },
    {
      "allowed": false,
      "auth_method": "Web",
      "first_at": 1444087505,
      "ip": "1.2.3.48",
      "last_at": 1444087505,
      "location": "Mukilteo, Washington"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-all-recent-access-attempts-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|401|Unauthorized||[global_error_response_schema](#schemaglobal_error_response_schema)|
|403|Forbidden||[global_error_response_schema](#schemaglobal_error_response_schema)|
|404|Not Found||[global_error_response_schema](#schemaglobal_error_response_schema)|
|500|Internal Server Error||Inline|

<h3 id="retrieve-all-recent-access-attempts-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|result|[object]|true|none|An array containing the IPs that recently attempted to access your account.|
|» allowed|boolean|true|none|Indicates if the IP address was granted access to the account.|
|» auth_method|string|true|none|The authentication method used when attempting access.|
|» first_at|integer|true|none|A Unix timestamp indicating when the first access attempt was made.|
|» ip|string|true|none|The IP addressed used during the access attempt.|
|» last_at|integer|true|none|A Unix timestamp indicating when the most recent access attempt was made|
|» location|string|true|none|The geographic location from which the access attempt originated.|

Status Code **500**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[object]|false|none|none|
|» message|string|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization

<a id="opIdGET_access_settings-whitelist"></a>

`GET /access_settings/whitelist`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of IP addresses that are currently allowed to access your account.**

Each IP address returned to you will have `created_at` and `updated_at` dates. Each IP will also be associated with an `id` that can be used to remove the address from your allow list.

## Add one or more IPs to the allow list

<a id="opIdPOST_access_settings-whitelist"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/access_settings/whitelist \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "ips": [
      {
        "ip": "192.168.1.1"
      },
      {
        "ip": "192.*.*.*"
      },
      {
        "ip": "192.168.1.3/32"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /access_settings/whitelist`

**This endpoint allows you to add one or more allowed IP addresses.**

To allow one or more IP addresses, pass them to this endpoint in an array. Once an IP address is added to your allow list, it will be assigned an `id` that can be used to remove the address. You can retrieve the ID associated with an IP using the "Retrieve a list of currently allowed IPs" endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ips": [
    {
      "ip": "192.168.1.1"
    },
    {
      "ip": "192.*.*.*"
    },
    {
      "ip": "192.168.1.3/32"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-one-or-more-ips-to-the-allow-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» ips|body|[object]|true|An array containing the IP(s) you want to allow.|
|» » ip|body|string|true|An IP address that you want to allow.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "result": [
    {
      "created_at": 1441824715,
      "id": 1,
      "ip": "192.168.1.1/32",
      "updated_at": 1441824715
    },
    {
      "created_at": 1441824715,
      "id": 2,
      "ip": "192.0.0.0/8",
      "updated_at": 1441824715
    },
    {
      "created_at": 1441824715,
      "id": 3,
      "ip": "192.168.1.3/32",
      "updated_at": 1441824715
    }
  ]
}
```

## Remove one or more IPs from the allow list

<a id="opIdDELETE_access_settings-whitelist"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/access_settings/whitelist \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "ids": [
      1,
      2,
      3
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /access_settings/whitelist`

**This endpoint allows you to remove one or more IP addresses from your list of allowed addresses.**

To remove one or more IP addresses, pass this endpoint an array containing the ID(s) associated with the IP(s) you intend to remove. You can retrieve the IDs associated with your allowed IP addresses using the "Retrieve a list of currently allowed IPs" endpoint.

It is possible to remove your own IP address, which will block access to your account. You will need to submit a [support ticket](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/support/) if this happens. For this reason, it is important to double check that you are removing only the IPs you intend to remove when using this endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ids": [
    1,
    2,
    3
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="remove-one-or-more-ips-from-the-allow-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» ids|body|[integer]|false|An array of the IDs of the IP address that you want to remove from your allow list.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
{}
```

> 401 Response

```json

    {
      "field": "field_name",

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-alerts">Alerts</h1>

## Retrieve all alerts

<a id="opIdGET_alerts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/alerts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /alerts`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve all of your alerts.**

Alerts allow you to specify an email address to receive notifications regarding your email usage or statistics. 
* Usage alerts allow you to set the threshold at which an alert will be sent.
* Stats notifications allow you to set how frequently you would like to receive email statistics reports. For example, "daily", "weekly", or "monthly".

For more information about alerts, please see our [Alerts documentation](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/alerts/).

<h3 id="retrieve-all-alerts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Authorization|header|string|false|none|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "created_at": 1451498784,
    "email_to": "example1@example.com",
    "id": 46,
    "percentage": 90,
    "type": "usage_limit",
    "updated_at": 1451498784
  },
  {
    "created_at": 1451498812,
    "email_to": "example2@example.com",
    "frequency": "monthly",
    "id": 47,
    "type": "stats_notification",
    "updated_at": 1451498812
  },
  {
    "created_at": 1451520930,
    "email_to": "example3@example.com",
    "frequency": "daily",
    "id": 48,
    "type": "stats_notification",
    "updated_at": 1451520930
  }
]
```

<h3 id="retrieve-all-alerts-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="retrieve-all-alerts-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» created_at|integer|true|none|A Unix timestamp indicating when the alert was created.|
|» email_to|string|true|none|The email address that the alert will be sent to.|
|» frequency|string|false|none|If the alert is of type stats_notification, this indicates how frequently the stats notifications will be sent. For example, "daily", "weekly", or "monthly".|
|» id|integer|true|none|The ID of the alert.|
|» percentage|integer|false|none|If the alert is of type usage_limit, this indicates the percentage of email usage that must be reached before the alert will be sent.|
|» type|string|true|none|The type of alert.|
|» updated_at|integer|false|none|A Unix timestamp indicating when the alert was last modified.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|usage_limit|
|» type|stats_notification|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization
</aside>

## Create a new Alert

<a id="opIdPOST_alerts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/alerts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "email_to": "example@example.com",
    "frequency": "daily",
    "type": "stats_notification"
  }'
```

`POST /alerts`

**This endpoint allows you to create a new alert.**

Alerts allow you to specify an email address to receive notifications regarding your email usage or statistics. There are two types of alerts that can be created with this endpoint:

* `usage_limit` allows you to set the threshold at which an alert will be sent.
* `stats_notification` allows you to set how frequently you would like to receive email statistics reports. For example, "daily", "weekly", or "monthly".

For more information about alerts, please see our [Alerts documentation](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/alerts/).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email_to": "example@example.com",
  "frequency": "daily",
  "type": "stats_notification"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Authorization|header|string|false|none|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» email_to|body|string(email) \| null|true|The email address the alert will be sent to.<br>Example: test@example.com|
|» frequency|body|string|false|Required for stats_notification. How frequently the alert will be sent.<br>Example: daily|
|» percentage|body|integer|false|Required for usage_alert. When this usage threshold is reached, the alert will be sent.<br>Example: 90|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of alert you want to create. Can be either usage_limit or stats_notification.<br>Example: usage_limit|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|stats_notification|
|» type|usage_limit|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "created_at": 1451520930,
  "email_to": "test@example.com",
  "frequency": "daily",
  "id": 48,
  "type": "stats_notification",
  "updated_at": 1451520930
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "field": "string",
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-alert-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request||Inline|

<h3 id="create-a-new-alert-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created_at|integer|true|none|A Unix timestamp indicating when the alert was created.|
|email_to|string(email)|true|none|The email address that the alert will be sent to.|
|frequency|string|false|none|If the alert is of type stats_notification, this indicates how frequently the stats notifications will be sent. For example, "daily", "weekly", or "monthly".|
|id|integer|true|none|The ID of the alert.|
|percentage|integer|false|none|"If the alert is of type usage_limit, this indicates the percentage of email usage that must be reached before the alert will be sent.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of alert.|

## Retrieve all API Keys belonging to the authenticated user

curl https://example.com/api_keys \

```

`GET /api_keys`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve all API Keys that belong to the authenticated user.**

A successful response from this API will include all available API keys' names and IDs.

For security reasons, there is not a way to retrieve the key itself after it's created. If you lose your API key, you must create a new one. Only the "Create API keys" endpoint will return a key to you and only at the time of creation.

An `api_key_id` can be used to update or delete the key, as well as retrieve the key's details, such as its scopes.

## Create API keys

<a id="opIdcreate-api-keys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api_keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My API Key",
    "scopes": [
      "mail.send",
      "alerts.create",
      "alerts.read"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api_keys`

**This endpoint allows you to create a new API Key for the user.**

To create your initial SendGrid API Key, you should [use the SendGrid App](https://app.sendgrid.com/settings/api_keys). Once you have created a first key with scopes to manage additional API keys, you can use this API for all other key management.

> There is a limit of 100 API Keys on your account.

A JSON request body containing a `name` property is required when making requests to this endpoint. If the number of maximum keys, 100, is reached, a `403` status will be returned.

Though the `name` field is required, it does not need to be unique. A unique API key ID will be generated for each key you create and returned in the response body.

It is not necessary to pass a `scopes` field to the API when creating a key, but you should be aware that omitting the `scopes` field from your request will create a key with "Full Access" permissions by default.

See the [API Key Permissions List](https://sendgrid.api-docs.io/v3.0/how-to-use-the-sendgrid-v3-api/api-authorization) for all available scopes. An API key's scopes can be updated after creation using the "Update API keys" endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My API Key",
  "scopes": [
    "mail.send",
    "alerts.create",
    "alerts.read"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-api-keys-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name you will use to describe this API Key.|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|The individual permissions that you are giving to this API Key.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "api_key": "SG.xxxxxxxx.yyyyyyyy",
  "api_key_id": "xxxxxxxx",
  "name": "My API Key",
  "scopes": [
    "mail.send",
    "alerts.create",
    "alerts.read"
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json

  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

    }
  ]

## Update API key name and scopes

<a id="opIdPUT_api_keys-api_key_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/api_keys/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Profiles key",
    "scopes": [
      "user.profile.read",
      "user.profile.update"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /api_keys/{api_key_id}`

**This endpoint allows you to update the name and scopes of a given API key.**

You must pass this endpoint a JSON request body with a `name` field and a `scopes` array containing at least one scope. The `name` and `scopes` fields will be used to update the key associated with the `api_key_id` in the request URL.

If you need to update a key's scopes only, pass the `name` field with the key's existing name; the `name` will not be modified. If you need to update a key's name only, use the "Update API key name" endpoint.

See the [API Key Permissions List](https://sendgrid.api-docs.io/v3.0/how-to-use-the-sendgrid-v3-api/api-authorization) for all available scopes.

> Body parameter

{

## Delete a Suppression Group

<a id="opIdDELETE_asm-groups-group_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/asm/groups/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /asm/groups/{group_id}`

**This endpoint allows you to delete a suppression group.**

If a recipient uses the "one-click unsubscribe" option on an email associated with a deleted group, that recipient will be added to the global suppression list.

Deleting a suppression group will remove the suppression, meaning email will once again be sent to the previously suppressed addresses. This should be avoided unless a recipient indicates they wish to receive email from you again. You can use our [bypass filters](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/sending-email/index-suppressions/#bypass-suppressions) to deliver messages to otherwise suppressed addresses when exceptions are required.

<h3 id="delete-a-suppression-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|group_id|path|string|true|The ID of the suppression group you would like to retrieve.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-suppression-group-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization
</aside>

`DELETE /asm/suppressions/global/{email}`

**This endpoint allows you to remove an email address from the global suppressions group.**

Deleting a suppression group will remove the suppression, meaning email will once again be sent to the previously suppressed addresses. This should be avoided unless a recipient indicates they wish to receive email from you again. You can use our [bypass filters](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/sending-email/index-suppressions/#bypass-suppressions) to deliver messages to otherwise suppressed addresses when exceptions are required.

<h3 id="delete-a-global-suppression-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|email|path|string|true|The email address of the global suppression you want to retrieve. Or, if you want to check if an email address is on the global suppressions list, enter that email address here.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-global-suppression-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization
</aside>

## Retrieve all global suppressions

<a id="opIdGET_suppression-unsubscribes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/suppression/unsubscribes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /suppression/unsubscribes`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of all email address that are globally suppressed.**

<h3 id="retrieve-all-global-suppressions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_time|query|integer|false|Refers start of the time range in unix timestamp when an unsubscribe email was created (inclusive).|
|end_time|query|integer|false|Refers end of the time range in unix timestamp when an unsubscribe email was created (inclusive).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results to display on each page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The point in the list of results to begin displaying global suppressions.|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

> 200 Response

  {

]

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-stats">Stats</h1>

## Retrieve email statistics by browser.

<a id="opIdGET_browsers-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/browsers/stats?start_date=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /browsers/stats`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve your email statistics segmented by browser type.**

**We only store up to 7 days of email activity in our database.** By default, 500 items will be returned per request via the Advanced Stats API endpoints.

Advanced Stats provide a more in-depth view of your email statistics and the actions taken by your recipients. You can segment these statistics by geographic location, device type, client type, browser, and mailbox provider. For more information about statistics, please see our [Statistics Overview](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/analytics-and-reporting/stats-overview/).

<h3 id="retrieve-email-statistics-by-browser-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|browsers|query|string|false|The browsers to get statistics for. You can include up to 10 different browsers by including this parameter multiple times.|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The point in the list to begin retrieving results.|
|aggregated_by|query|string|false|How to group the statistics. Must be either "day", "week", or "month".|
|start_date|query|string|true|The starting date of the statistics to retrieve. Must follow format YYYY-MM-DD.|
|end_date|query|string|false|The end date of the statistics to retrieve. Defaults to today. Must follow format YYYY-MM-DD.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|aggregated_by|day|
|aggregated_by|week|
|aggregated_by|month|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "date": "2014-10-01",
    "stats": [
      {
        "metrics": {
          "clicks": 0,
          "unique_clicks": 0
        },
        "name": "Chrome",
        "type": "browser"
      },
      {
        "metrics": {
          "clicks": 1,
          "unique_clicks": 1
        },
        "name": "Firefox",
        "type": "browser"
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "date": "2014-10-02",
    "stats": [
      {
        "metrics": {
          "clicks": 0,
          "unique_clicks": 0
        },
        "name": "Chrome",
        "type": "browser"
      },
      {
        "metrics": {
          "clicks": 1,
          "unique_clicks": 1
        },
        "name": "Firefox",
        "type": "browser"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="retrieve-email-statistics-by-browser-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|

<h3 id="retrieve-email-statistics-by-country-and-stateprovince-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» date|string|false|none|The date that the statistics were gathered.|
|» stats|[object]|false|none|The list of statistics.|
|» » metrics|[advanced_stats_clicks_opens](#schemaadvanced_stats_clicks_opens)|false|none|The individual events and their stats.|
|» » name|string|false|none|The name of the specific segmentation.|
|» » type|string|false|none|The type of segmentation.|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization
</aside>

## Retrieve email statistics by mailbox provider.

<a id="opIdGET_mailbox_providers-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/mailbox_providers/stats?start_date=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /mailbox_providers/stats`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve your email statistics segmented by recipient mailbox provider.**

**We only store up to 7 days of email activity in our database.** By default, 500 items will be returned per request via the Advanced Stats API endpoints.

Advanced Stats provide a more in-depth view of your email statistics and the actions taken by your recipients. You can segment these statistics by geographic location, device type, client type, browser, and mailbox provider. For more information about statistics, please see our [Statistics Overview](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/analytics-and-reporting/stats-overview/).

<h3 id="retrieve-email-statistics-by-mailbox-provider-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|mailbox_providers|query|string|false|The mail box providers to get statistics for. You can include up to 10 by including this parameter multiple times.|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The point in the list to begin retrieving results.|
|aggregated_by|query|string|false|How to group the statistics. Must be either "day", "week", or "month".|
|start_date|query|string|true|The starting date of the statistics to retrieve. Must follow format YYYY-MM-DD.|
|end_date|query|string|false|The end date of the statistics to retrieve. Defaults to today. Must follow format YYYY-MM-DD.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|aggregated_by|day|
|aggregated_by|week|
|aggregated_by|month|

## Retrieve global email statistics

<a id="opIdGET_stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/stats?start_date=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /stats`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve all of your global email statistics between a given date range.**

Parent accounts will see aggregated stats for their account and all subuser accounts. Subuser accounts will only see their own stats.

<h3 id="retrieve-global-email-statistics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The point in the list to begin retrieving results.|
|aggregated_by|query|string|false|How to group the statistics. Must be either "day", "week", or "month".|
|start_date|query|string|true|The starting date of the statistics to retrieve. Must follow format YYYY-MM-DD.|
|end_date|query|string|false|The end date of the statistics to retrieve. Defaults to today. Must follow format YYYY-MM-DD.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|aggregated_by|day|
|aggregated_by|week|
|aggregated_by|month|

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-campaigns-api">Campaigns API</h1>

## Retrieve all Campaigns

<a id="opIdGET_campaigns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/campaigns \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /campaigns`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of all of your campaigns.**

Returns campaigns in reverse order they were created (newest first).

Returns an empty array if no campaigns exist.

<h3 id="retrieve-all-campaigns-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results you would like to receive at a time.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The index of the first campaign to return, where 0 is the first campaign.|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": [
    {
      "categories": [
        "spring line"
      ],
      "custom_unsubscribe_url": "",
      "html_content": "<html><head><title></title></head><body><p>Check out our spring line!</p></body></html>",
      "id": 986724,
      "ip_pool": "marketing",
      "list_ids": [
        110,
        124
      ],
      "plain_content": "Check out our spring line!",
      "segment_ids": [
        110
      ],
      "sender_id": 124451,
      "status": "Draft",
      "subject": "New Products for Spring!",
      "suppression_group_id": 42,
      "title": "March Newsletter"
    },
    {
      "categories": [
        "winter line"
      ],
      "custom_unsubscribe_url": "",
      "html_content": "<html><head><title></title></head><body><p>Last call for winter clothes!</p></body></html>",
      "id": 986723,
      "ip_pool": "marketing",
      "list_ids": [

      ],

      ],
      "sender_id": 124451,
      "status": "Sent",
      "subject": "Final Winter Product Sale!",
      "suppression_group_id": 42,
      "title": "February Newsletter"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Create a Campaign

<a id="opIdPOST_campaigns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/campaigns \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "categories": [
      "summer line"
    ],
    "custom_unsubscribe_url": "",
    "html_content": "<html><head><title></title></head><body><p>Check out our summer line!</p></body></html>",
    "id": 986724,
    "ip_pool": "marketing",
    "list_ids": [
      110,
      124
    ],
    "plain_content": "Check out our summer line!",
    "segment_ids": [
      110
    ],
    "sender_id": 124451,
    "status": "Draft",
    "subject": "New Products for Summer!",
    "suppression_group_id": 42,
    "title": "May Newsletter"
  }'
```

`POST /campaigns`

**This endpoint allows you to create a campaign.**

In order to send or schedule the campaign, you will be required to provide a subject, sender ID, content (we suggest both html and plain text), and at least one list or segment ID. This information is not required when you create a campaign.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "categories": [
    "summer line"
  ],
  "custom_unsubscribe_url": "",
  "html_content": "<html><head><title></title></head><body><p>Check out our summer line!</p></body></html>",
  "id": 986724,
  "ip_pool": "marketing",
  "list_ids": [
    110,
    124
  ],
  "plain_content": "Check out our summer line!",
  "segment_ids": [
    110
  ],
  "sender_id": 124451,
  "status": "Draft",
  "subject": "New Products for Summer!",
  "suppression_group_id": 42,
  "title": "May Newsletter"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-campaign-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[campaign_request](#schemacampaign_request)|false|none|
|» categories|body|[string]|false|The categories you would like associated to this campaign.|
|» custom_unsubscribe_url|body|string \| null|false|This is the url of the custom unsubscribe page that you provide for customers to unsubscribe from your suppression groups.|
|» editor|body|string|false|The editor used in the UI.|
|» html_content|body|string \| null|false|The HTML of your marketing email.|
|» ip_pool|body|string \| null|false|The pool of IPs that you would like to send this email from.|
|» list_ids|body|[integer]|false|The IDs of the lists you are sending this campaign to. You can have both segment IDs and list IDs|
|» plain_content|body|string \| null|false|The plain text content of your emails.|
|» segment_ids|body|[integer]|false|The segment IDs that you are sending this list to. You can have both segment IDs and list IDs. Segments are limited to 10 segment IDs.|
|» sender_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the "sender" identity that you have created. Your recipients will see this as the "from" on your marketing emails.|
|» subject|body|string \| null|false|The subject of your campaign that your recipients will see.|
|» suppression_group_id|body|integer \| null|false|The suppression group that this marketing email belongs to, allowing recipients to opt-out of emails of this type.|
|» title|body|string|true|The display title of your campaign. This will be viewable by you in the Marketing Campaigns UI.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» editor|code|
|» editor|design|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "categories": [
    "spring line"
  ],
  "custom_unsubscribe_url": "",
  "html_content": "<html><head><title></title></head><body><p>Check out our spring line!</p></body></html>",
  "id": 986724,
  "ip_pool": "marketing",
  "list_ids": [
    110,
    124
  ],
  "plain_content": "Check out our spring line!",
  "segment_ids": [
    110
  ],
  "sender_id": 124451,
  "status": "Draft",
  "subject": "New Products for Spring!",
  "suppression_group_id": 42,
  "title": "March Newsletter"
}
```

```json

## Schedule a Campaign

<a id="opIdPOST_campaigns-campaign_id-schedules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/campaigns/0/schedules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "send_at": 1489771528
  }'
```

`POST /campaigns/{campaign_id}/schedules`

**This endpoint allows you to schedule a specific date and time for your campaign to be sent.**

If you have the flexibility, it's better to schedule mail for off-peak times. Most emails are scheduled and sent at the top of the hour or half hour. Scheduling email to avoid those times (for example, scheduling at 10:53) can result in lower deferral rates because it won't be going through our servers at the same times as everyone else's mail.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "send_at": 1489771528
}
```

<h3 id="schedule-a-campaign-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|campaign_id|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» send_at|body|integer|true|The unix timestamp for the date and time you would like your campaign to be sent out.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 1234,
  "send_at": 1489771528,
  "status": "Scheduled"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "subject",
      "message": "subject can't be blank"
    },
    {
      "field": "sender_id",
      "message": "sender_id can't be blank"
    },
    {
      "field": "plain_content",
      "message": "plain_content can't be blank, please provide plain text or html content"
    },
    {
      "field": "list_id",
      "message": "You must select at least 1 segment or 1 list to send to."
    },
    {
      "field": "unsubscribe_tag",
      "message": "An [unsubscribe] tag in both your html and plain content is required to send a campaign."
    },
    {
      "field": "suppression_group_id",
      "message": "Either a suppression_group_id or custom_unsubscribe_url is required to send a campaign."
    },
    {
      "field": null,
      "message": "You do not have enough credits to send this campaign. Upgrade your plan to send more: https://app.sendgrid.com/settings/billing"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

  "errors": [
    {
      "field": null,
      "message": "authorization required"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json

  "errors": [
    {
      "field": null,
      "message": "You cannot POST to a campaign that has already sent or scheduled. However you can update a scheduled campaign with a PATCH."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

    {

    }
  ]
}

Please set one of these values before sending a test."<br>"sender_id": "Please assign a sender identity to your campaign before sending a test."|[global_error_response_schema](#schemaglobal_error_response_schema)|
|404|Not Found|"": "not found"|[global_error_response_schema](#schemaglobal_error_response_schema)|

|to|string|true|none|none|

## Retrieve Email Statistics for Categories

<a id="opIdGET_categories-stats"></a>

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/categories/stats?start_date=string&categories=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /categories/stats`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve all of your email statistics for each of your categories.**

If you do not define any query parameters, this endpoint will return a sum for each category in groups of 10.

<h3 id="retrieve-email-statistics-for-categories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|end_date|query|string|false|The end date of the statistics to retrieve. Defaults to today. Must follow format YYYY-MM-DD.|
|categories|query|string|true|The individual categories that you want to retrieve statistics for. You may include up to 10 different categories.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of results to include.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The number of results to skip.|
|aggregated_by|query|string|false|How to group the statistics. Must be either "day", "week", or "month".|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

## Retrieve sums of email stats for each category [Needs: Stats object defined, has category ID?]

```

`GET /categories/stats/sums`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve the total sum of each email statistic for every category over the given date range.**

If you do not define any query parameters, this endpoint will return a sum for each category in groups of 10.

<h3 id="retrieve-sums-of-email-stats-for-each-category-needs-stats-object-defined-has-category-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|sort_by_direction|query|string|false|The direction you want to sort.|
|start_date|query|string|true|The starting date of the statistics to retrieve. Must follow format YYYY-MM-DD.|
|end_date|query|string|false|The end date of the statistics to retrieve. Defaults to today. Must follow format YYYY-MM-DD.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of results returned.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The point in the list to begin retrieving results.|
|aggregated_by|query|string|false|How to group the statistics. Must be either "day", "week", or "month".|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_by_direction|desc|
|sort_by_direction|asc|
|aggregated_by|day|
|aggregated_by|week|
|aggregated_by|month|

```bash
curl https://example.com/contactdb/custom_fields \

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "pet",
    "type": "text"
  }'
```

`POST /contactdb/custom_fields`

**This endpoint allows you to create a custom field.**

**You can create up to 120 custom fields.**

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "pet",
  "type": "text"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-custom-field-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» type|body|string|false|none|

  "id": 1,
  "name": "pet",
  "type": "text"
}
```

  "errors": [
    {
      "field": null,
      "message": "Returned if request body is invalid JSON"
    },
    {
      "field": "type",
      "message": "Returned if custom field type is invalid or not provided"
    },
    {
      "field": "name",
      "message": "Returned if custom field name is not provided"
    }
  ]
}

`GET /contactdb/recipients`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve all of your Marketing Campaigns recipients.**

Batch deletion of a page makes it possible to receive an empty page of recipients before reaching the end of
the list of recipients. To avoid this issue; iterate over pages until a 404 is retrieved.

<h3 id="retrieve-recipients-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|Page index of first recipients to return (must be a positive integer)|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Number of recipients to return at a time (must be a positive integer between 1 and 1000)|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "recipients": [
    {}
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": null,
      "message": "authorization required"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|"page" : "Returned if page is not a valid integer"<br>"page" : "Returned if page is less than 1"<br>"page_size" : "Returned if page_size is not a valid integer"<br>"page_size" : "Returned if page_size is less than 1 or greater than 1000"|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized||[global_error_response_schema](#schemaglobal_error_response_schema)|

`POST /contactdb/recipients`

**This endpoint allows you to add a Marketing Campaigns recipient.**

You can add custom field data as a parameter on this endpoint. We have provided an example using some of the default custom fields SendGrid provides.

The rate limit is three requests every 2 seconds. You can upload 1000  contacts per request. So the maximum upload rate is 1500 recipients per second.

## Search recipients

<a id="opIdGET_contactdb-recipients-search"></a>

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /contactdb/recipients/search`

**This endpoint allows you to perform a search on all of your Marketing Campaigns recipients.**

field_name:

* is a variable that is substituted for your actual custom field name from your recipient.
* Text fields must be url-encoded. Date fields are searchable only by unix timestamp (e.g. 2/2/2015 becomes 1422835200)
* If field_name is a 'reserved' date field, such as created_at or updated_at, the system will internally convert
your epoch time to a date range encompassing the entire day. For example, an epoch time of 1422835600 converts to
Mon, 02 Feb 2015 00:06:40 GMT, but internally the system will search from Mon, 02 Feb 2015 00:00:00 GMT through
Mon, 02 Feb 2015 23:59:59 GMT.

<h3 id="search-recipients-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

}

## Search recipients

<a id="opIdPOST_contactdb-recipients-search"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/contactdb/recipients/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "conditions": [
      {
        "and_or": "",
        "field": "birthday",
        "operator": "eq",
        "value": "01/12/1985"
      },
      {
        "and_or": "",
        "field": "birthday",
        "operator": "eq",
        "value": "01/12/1985"
      },
      {
        "and_or": "",
        "field": "birthday",
        "operator": "eq",
        "value": "01/12/1985"
      },
      {
        "and_or": "",
        "field": "birthday",
        "operator": "eq",
        "value": "01/12/1985"
      }
    ],
    "list_id": -27497588
  }'
```

`POST /contactdb/recipients/search`

<p>
  Search using segment conditions without actually creating a segment.
  Body contains a JSON object with <code>conditions</code>, a list of conditions as described below, and an optional <code>list_id</code>, which is a valid list ID for a list to limit the search on.
</p>

<p>
  Valid operators for create and update depend on the type of the field for which you are searching.
</p>

<ul>
  <li>Dates:
    <ul>
      <li>"eq", "ne", "lt" (before), "gt" (after)
        <ul>
          <li>You may use MM/DD/YYYY for day granularity or an epoch for second granularity.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
      <li>"empty", "not_empty"</li>
      <li>"is within"
        <ul>
          <li>You may use an <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601">ISO 8601 date format</a> or the # of days.</li>
        </ul>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>Text: "contains", "eq" (is - matches the full field), "ne" (is not - matches any field where the entire field is not the condition value), "empty", "not_empty"</li>
  <li>Numbers: "eq", "lt", "gt", "empty", "not_empty"</li>
  <li>Email Clicks and Opens: "eq" (opened), "ne" (not opened)</li>
</ul>

<p>
  Field values must all be a string.
</p>

<p>
  Search conditions using "eq" or "ne" for email clicks and opens should provide a "field" of either <code>clicks.campaign_identifier</code> or <code>opens.campaign_identifier</code>.
  The condition value should be a string containing the id of a completed campaign.
</p>

<p>
  Search conditions list may contain multiple conditions, joined by an "and" or "or" in the "and_or" field.
  The first condition in the conditions list must have an empty "and_or", and subsequent conditions must all specify an "and_or".
</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conditions": [
    {
      "and_or": "",
      "field": "birthday",
      "operator": "eq",
      "value": "01/12/1985"
    },
    {
      "and_or": "",
      "field": "birthday",
      "operator": "eq",
      "value": "01/12/1985"
    },
    {
      "and_or": "",
      "field": "birthday",
      "operator": "eq",
      "value": "01/12/1985"
    },
    {
      "and_or": "",
      "field": "birthday",
      "operator": "eq",
      "value": "01/12/1985"
    }
  ],
  "list_id": -27497588
}
```

<h3 id="search-recipients-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» conditions|body|[object]|true|none|
|» list_id|body|integer(int32)|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "recipient_count": 65190677,
  "recipients": [
    {
      "created_at": -27901208,

    },

## Create a Segment

<a id="opIdPOST_contactdb-segments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/contactdb/segments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "conditions": [
      {
        "and_or": "",
        "field": "last_name",
        "operator": "eq",
        "value": "Miller"
      },
      {
        "and_or": "and",
        "field": "last_clicked",
        "operator": "gt",
        "value": "01/02/2015"
      },
      {
        "and_or": "or",
        "field": "clicks.campaign_identifier",
        "operator": "eq",
        "value": "513"
      }
    ],
    "list_id": 4,
    "name": "Last Name Miller",
    "recipient_count": 1234
  }'
```

`POST /contactdb/segments`

**This endpoint allows you to create a new segment.**


  Valid operators for create and update depend on the type of the field for which you are searching.

**Dates**
- "eq", "ne", "lt" (before), "gt" (after)
    - You may use MM/DD/YYYY for day granularity or an epoch for second granularity.
- "empty", "not_empty"
- "is within"
    - You may use an [ISO 8601 date format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) or the # of days.

**Text**
- "contains"
- "eq" (is/equals - matches the full field)
- "ne" (is not/not equals - matches any field where the entire field is not the condition value)
- "empty"
- "not_empty"

**Numbers**
- "eq" (is/equals)
- "lt" (is less than)
- "gt" (is greater than)
- "empty"
- "not_empty"

**Email Clicks and Opens**
- "eq" (opened)
- "ne" (not opened)

All field values must be a string.


Conditions using "eq" or "ne" for email clicks and opens should provide a "field" of either `clicks.campaign_identifier` or `opens.campaign_identifier`.
The condition value should be a string containing the id of a completed campaign.


The conditions list may contain multiple conditions, joined by an "and" or "or" in the "and_or" field.

The first condition in the conditions list must have an empty "and_or", and subsequent conditions must all specify an "and_or".

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conditions": [
    {
      "and_or": "",
      "field": "last_name",
      "operator": "eq",
      "value": "Miller"
    },
    {
      "and_or": "and",
      "field": "last_clicked",
      "operator": "gt",
      "value": "01/02/2015"
    },
    {
      "and_or": "or",
      "field": "clicks.campaign_identifier",
      "operator": "eq",
      "value": "513"
    }
  ],
  "list_id": 4,
  "name": "Last Name Miller",
  "recipient_count": 1234
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-segment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[contactdb_segments](#schemacontactdb_segments)|false|none|
|» conditions|body|[[contactdb_segments_conditions](#schemacontactdb_segments_conditions)]|true|The conditions for a recipient to be included in this segment.|
|» list_id|body|integer|false|The list id from which to make this segment. Not including this ID will mean your segment is created from the main contactdb rather than a list.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of this segment.|
|» recipient_count|body|number|false|The count of recipients in this list. This is not included on creation of segments.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "conditions": [
    {
      "and_or": "",
      "field": "last_name",
      "operator": "eq",
      "value": "Miller"
    },
    {
      "and_or": "and",
      "field": "last_clicked",
      "operator": "gt",
      "value": "01/02/2015"
    },
    {
      "and_or": "or",
      "field": "clicks.campaign_identifier",
      "operator": "eq",
      "value": "513"
    }
  ],
  "id": 1,
  "list_id": 4,
  "name": "Last Name Miller",
  "recipient_count": 0
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "request body is not valid json"
    },
    {
      "message": "invalid value is passed into one of the request body parameters"
    },
    {
      "field": "field",
      "message": "field and set value is not passed into the request body"
    },
    {
      "field": "value",
      "message": "value and set value is not passed into the request body"
    },
    {
      "field": "operator",
      "message": "operator and set value is not passed into the request body"
    },
    {
      "field": "and_or",
      "message": "and_or is not set on more than one condition and less than all conditions"
    },
    {

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-designs-api">Designs API</h1>

## List Designs

<a id="opIdLIST-designs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/designs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /designs`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of designs already stored in your Design Library**.

A GET request to `/designs` will return a list of your existing designs. This endpoint will not return the pre-built Twilio SendGrid designs. Pre-built designs can be retrieved using the `/designs/pre-builts` endpoint, which is detailed below.

By default, you will receive 100 results per request; however, you can modify the number of results returned by passing an integer to the `page_size` query parameter.

<h3 id="list-designs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_size|query|integer|false|number of results to return|
|page_token|query|string|false|token corresponding to a specific page of results, as provided by metadata|
|summary|query|boolean|false|set to false to return all fields|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "_metadata": {
    "count": 3,
    "self": "https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/designs?page_token=vHdvHCg0w1F-TmWJcPNpTEnFY2aPEmRBHONwOgZ6TgJbX2_I"
  },
  "result": [
    {
      "categories": [
        "welcome",
        "new customer"
      ],
      "created_at": "2021-04-09T17:29:46Z",

`POST /designs`

**This endpoint allows you to create a new design**.

You can add a new design by passing data, including a string of HTML email content, to `/designs`. When creating designs from scratch, be aware of the styling constraints inherent to many email clients. For a list of best practices, see our guide to [Cross-Platform Email Design](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/sending-email/cross-platform-html-design/).

The Design Library can also convert your design’s HTML elements into drag and drop modules that are editable in the Designs Library user interface. For more, visit the [Design and Code Editor documentation](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/sending-email/editor/#drag--drop-markup).

Because the `/designs` endpoint makes it easy to add designs, you can create a design with your preferred tooling or migrate designs you already own without relying on the Design Library UI.

<h3 id="create-design-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[design-input](#schemadesign-input)|false|none|
|» editor|body|string|false|The editor used in the UI.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the new design.|
|» editor|body|string|false|The editor used in the UI.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the new design.|
|» categories|body|[string]|false|The list of categories applied to the design|
|» generate_plain_content|body|boolean|false|If true, plain_content is always generated from html_content. If false, plain_content is not altered.|
|» subject|body|string|false|Subject of the Design.|
|» html_content|body|string|true|The HTML content of the Design.|
|» plain_content|body|string|false|Plain text content of the Design.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» editor|code|
|» editor|design|
|» editor|code|
|» editor|design|

## List SendGrid Pre-built Designs

<a id="opIdLIST-Sendgrid-Pre-built-designs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/designs/pre-builts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /designs/pre-builts`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of pre-built designs provided by Twilio SendGrid**.

Unlike the `/designs` endpoint where *your* designs are stored, a GET request made to `designs/pre-builts` will retrieve a list of the pre-built Twilio SendGrid designs. This endpoint will not return the designs stored in your Design Library.

By default, you will receive 100 results per request; however, you can modify the number of results returned by passing an integer to the `page_size` query parameter.

This endpoint is useful for retrieving the IDs of Twilio SendGrid designs that you want to duplicate and modify.

<h3 id="list-sendgrid-pre-built-designs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_size|query|integer|false|number of results to return|
|page_token|query|string|false|token corresponding to a specific page of results, as provided by metadata|
|summary|query|boolean|false|set to false to return all fields|

## Get SendGrid Pre-built Design

<a id="opIdGET-sendgrid-pre-built-design"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/designs/pre-builts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /designs/pre-builts/{id}`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve a single pre-built design**.

A GET request to `/designs/pre-builts/{id}` will retrieve details about a specific pre-built design.

This endpoint is valuable when retrieving details about a pre-built design that you wish to duplicate and modify.

<h3 id="get-sendgrid-pre-built-design-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the pre-built Design you want to duplicate.|

## Duplicate SendGrid Pre-built Design

<a id="opIdPOST-sendgrid-pre-built-design"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/designs/pre-builts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "editor": "design",
    "name": "Ahoy, Cake or Pie Cafe!"
  }'
```

`POST /designs/pre-builts/{id}`

**This endpoint allows you to duplicate one of the pre-built Twilio SendGrid designs**.

Like duplicating one of your existing designs, you are not required to pass any data in the body of a request to this endpoint. If you choose to leave the `name` field blank, your duplicate will be assigned the name of the design it was copied from with the text "Duplicate: " prepended to it. This name change is only a convenience, as the duplicate design will be assigned a unique ID that differentiates it from your other designs. You can retrieve the IDs for Twilio SendGrid pre-built designs using the "List SendGrid Pre-built Designs" endpoint.

You can modify your duplicate’s name at the time of creation by passing an updated value to the `name` field when making the initial request.
More on retrieving design IDs can be found above.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "editor": "design",
  "name": "Ahoy, Cake or Pie Cafe!"
}
```

<h3 id="duplicate-sendgrid-pre-built-design-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the pre-built Design you want to duplicate.|
|body|body|[design-duplicate-input](#schemadesign-duplicate-input)|false|none|
|» editor|body|string|false|The editor used in the UI.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the new design.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» editor|code|
|» editor|design|

`GET /designs/{id}`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve a single design**.

A GET request to `/designs/{id}` will retrieve details about a specific design in your Design Library.

This endpoint is valuable when retrieving information stored in a field that you wish to update using a PATCH request.

## Duplicate Design

<a id="opIdPOST-design"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/designs/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "editor": "design",
    "name": "Ahoy, Cake or Pie Cafe!"
  }'
```

`POST /designs/{id}`

**This endpoint allows you to duplicate one of your existing designs**.

Modifying an existing design is often the easiest way to create something new.

You are not required to pass any data in the body of a request to this endpoint. If you choose to leave the `name` field blank, your duplicate will be assigned the name of the design it was copied from with the text "Duplicate: " prepended to it. This name change is only a convenience, as the duplicate will be assigned a unique ID that differentiates it from your other designs.

You can modify your duplicate’s name at the time of creation by passing an updated value to the `name` field when making the initial request.
More on retrieving design IDs can be found below.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "editor": "design",
  "name": "Ahoy, Cake or Pie Cafe!"
}
```

<h3 id="duplicate-design-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the Design you want to duplicate.|
|body|body|[design-duplicate-input](#schemadesign-duplicate-input)|false|none|
|» editor|body|string|false|The editor used in the UI.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the new design.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» editor|code|
|» editor|design|

`PATCH /designs/{id}`

**This endpoint allows you to edit a design**.

The Design API supports PATCH requests, which allow you to make partial updates to a single design. Passing data to a specific field will update only the data stored in that field; all other fields will be unaltered.

For example, updating a design's name requires that you make a PATCH request to this endpoint with data specified for the `name` field only.

```
{
    "name": "<Updated Name>"
}
```

<h3 id="update-design-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the Design you want to duplicate.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» categories|body|[string]|false|The list of categories applied to the design|
|» generate_plain_content|body|boolean|false|If true, plain_content is always generated from html_content. If false, plain_content is not altered.|
|» html_content|body|string|false|The HTML content of the Design.|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the Design.|
|» plain_content|body|string|false|Plain text content of the Design.|
|» subject|body|string|false|Subject of the Design.|

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-ip-addresses">IP Addresses</h1>

## Retrieve all IP addresses

<a id="opIdGET_ips"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/ips \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /ips`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of all assigned and unassigned IPs.**

Response includes warm up status, pools, assigned subusers, and reverse DNS info. The start_date field corresponds to when warmup started for that IP.

A single IP address or a range of IP addresses may be dedicated to an account in order to send email for multiple domains. The reputation of this IP is based on the aggregate performance of all the senders who use it.

<h3 id="retrieve-all-ip-addresses-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ip|query|string|false|The IP address to get|
|exclude_whitelabels|query|boolean|false|Should we exclude reverse DNS records (whitelabels)?|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of IPs you want returned at the same time.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The offset for the number of IPs that you are requesting.|
|subuser|query|string|false|The subuser you are requesting for.|
|sort_by_direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort the results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_by_direction|desc|
|sort_by_direction|asc|

> Example responses

```json

  {

    "ip": "192.168.1.1",
    "pools": [
      "pool1",
      "pool2"
    ],

      "tim@sendgrid.net"
    ],

    "start_date": 1409616000,
    "subusers": [],
    "warmup": false,
    "whitelabeled": true
  }
]
```

## Add an IP address to a pool

<a id="opIdPOST_ips-pools-pool_name-ips"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/ips/pools/string/ips \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "ip": "0.0.0.0"
  }'
```

`POST /ips/pools/{pool_name}/ips`

**This endpoint allows you to add an IP address to an IP pool.**

You can add the same IP address to multiple pools. It may take up to 60 seconds for your IP address to be added to a pool after your request is made.

Before you can add an IP to a pool, you need to activate it in your SendGrid account:

1. Log into your SendGrid account.  
1. Navigate to **Settings** and then select **IP Addresses**.  
1. Find the IP address you want to activate and then click **Edit**.  
1. Check **Allow my account to send mail using this IP address**.
1. Click **Save**.

You can retrieve all of your available IP addresses from the "Retrieve all IP addresses" endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ip": "0.0.0.0"
}
```

<h3 id="add-an-ip-address-to-a-pool-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pool_name|path|string|true|The name of the IP pool you want to add the address to. If the name contains spaces, they must be URL encoded (e.g., "Test Pool" becomes "Test%20Pool").|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» ip|body|string|false|The IP address that you want to add to the named pool.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "ip": "000.00.00.0",
  "pools": [
    "test1"
  ],
  "start_date": 1409616000,
  "warmup": true
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": null,
      "message": "resource not found"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-an-ip-address-to-a-pool-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|
|404|Not Found||Inline|

<h3 id="add-an-ip-address-to-a-pool-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ip|string|true|none|The IP address.|
|pools|[string]|true|none|The IP pools that this IP address has been added to.|
|start_date|integer|true|none|A Unix timestamp indicating when the warmup process began for the added IP address.|
|warmup|boolean|true|none|Indicates if the IP address is in warmup.|

Status Code **404**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[object]|false|none|The error returned.|
|» field|object \| null|false|none|none|
|» message|string|false|none|A message explaining why the IP address could not be added to the IP Pool.|

## Cancel or pause a scheduled send

<a id="opIdPOST_user-scheduled_sends"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/scheduled_sends \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "batch_id": "YOUR_BATCH_ID",
    "status": "pause"
  }'
```

`POST /user/scheduled_sends`

**This endpoint allows you to cancel or pause a scheduled send associated with a `batch_id`.**

Passing this endpoint a `batch_id` and status will cancel or pause the scheduled send.

Once a scheduled send is set to `pause` or `cancel` you must use the "Update a scheduled send" endpoint to change its status or the "Delete a cancellation or pause from a scheduled send" endpoint to remove the status. Passing a status change to a scheduled send that has already been paused or cancelled will result in a `400` level status code.

If the maximum number of cancellations/pauses are added to a send, a `400` level status code will be returned.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "batch_id": "YOUR_BATCH_ID",
  "status": "pause"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» batch_id|body|string|true|The batch ID is the identifier that your scheduled mail sends share.|
|» status|body|string|true|The status of the send you would like to implement. This can be pause or cancel. To delete a pause or cancel status see DELETE /v3/user/scheduled_sends/{batch_id}|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|pause|
|» status|cancel|

> 201 Response

  "batch_id": "HkJ5yLYULb7Rj8GKSx7u025ouWVlMgAi",
  "status": "pause"
}

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-mail-send">Mail Send</h1>

`POST /mail/send`

The Mail Send endpoint allows you to send email over SendGrid’s v3 Web API, the most recent version of our API. If you are looking for documentation about the v2 Mail Send endpoint, see our [v2 API Reference](https://sendgrid.com/docs/API_Reference/Web_API/mail.html).

## Helper Libraries

Twilio SendGrid provides libraries to help you quickly and easily integrate with the v3 Web API in 7 different languages:

* [C#](https://github.com/sendgrid/sendgrid-csharp) 
* [Go](https://github.com/sendgrid/sendgrid-go)
* [Java](https://github.com/sendgrid/sendgrid-java)
* [Node JS](https://github.com/sendgrid/sendgrid-nodejs)
* [PHP](https://github.com/sendgrid/sendgrid-php)
* [Python](https://github.com/sendgrid/sendgrid-python)
* [Ruby](https://github.com/sendgrid/sendgrid-ruby)

## Dynamic Transactional Templates and Handlebars

In order to send a dynamic template, specify the template ID with the `template_id` parameter. 

To specify handlebar substitutions, define your substitutions in the request JSON with this syntax:

```
"dynamic_template_data": {
      "guest": "Jane Doe",
      "partysize": "4",
      "english": true,
      "date": "April 1st, 2021"
    }
```

For more information about Dynamic Transactional Templates and Handlebars, see our documentation and reference pages.

* [How to send an email with Dynamic Transactional Templates
](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/sending-email/how-to-send-an-email-with-dynamic-transactional-templates/)
* [Using Handlebars](https://sendgrid.com/docs/for-developers/sending-email/using-handlebars/) 

## Mail Body Compression

Mail body compression is available to some high volume accounts. Talk to your CSM if you are interested in this functionality. Mail body compression works by setting up a JSON payload as defined on this page, then compressing it with gzip (the gzip file can be no more than 30mb).

To use mail body compression:

1. Add a `Content-Encoding` header, with a value of `gzip`.  
   a. `Content-Encoding: gzip` 
2. Send the gzip as a data-binary.  
   a. `--data-binary '@data.json.gz'
`

## Multiple Reply-To Emails

Using `reply_to_list` allows senders to include more than one recipient email address to receive reply and/or bounce messages from the recipient of the email.

### Usage Considerations

* `reply_to` is mutually exclusive with `reply_to_list`. If both are used, then the API call will be rejected. 
* The `reply_to_list` object, when used, must at least have an email parameter and may also contain a name parameter.
* Each email address in the `reply_to_list` should be unique.
* There is a limit of 1000 `reply_to_list` emails per mail/send request.
* In SMTP calls, we will omit any invalid emails.

### Possible 400 Error Messages

* `reply_to` is mutually exclusive with `reply_to_list`.
* The `reply_to_list` object, when used, must at least have an email parameter and may also contain a name parameter.
* Each email address in the `reply_to_list` should be unique.
* There is a limit of X `reply_to` emails per mail/send request.
* The `reply_to_list` email does not contain a valid address.
* The `reply_to_list` email exceeds the maximum total length of X characters.
* The `reply_to_list` email parameter is required.

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-settings---mail">Settings - Mail</h1>

## Retrieve all mail settings

<a id="opIdGET_mail_settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/mail_settings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /mail_settings`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of all mail settings.**

Each setting will be returned with an `enabled` status set to `true` or `false` and a short description that explains what the setting does.

<h3 id="retrieve-all-mail-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of settings to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Where in the list of results to begin displaying settings.|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

> Example responses

## Retrieve address whitelist mail settings

<a id="opIdGET_mail_settings-address_whitelist"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/mail_settings/address_whitelist \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /mail_settings/address_whitelist`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve your current email address whitelist settings.**

The Address Whitelist setting allows you to specify email addresses or domains for which mail should never be suppressed.

For example, if you own the domain `example.com`, and one or more of your recipients use `email@example.com` addresses, placing `example.com` in the address whitelist setting instructs Twilio SendGrid to ignore all bounces, blocks, and unsubscribes logged for that domain. In other words, all bounces, blocks, and unsubscribes will still be sent to `example.com` as if they were sent under normal sending conditions.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Update address whitelist mail settings

<a id="opIdPATCH_mail_settings-address_whitelist"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/mail_settings/address_whitelist \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "list": [
      "email1@example.com",
      "example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /mail_settings/address_whitelist`

**This endpoint allows you to update your current email address whitelist settings.**

You can select whether or not this setting should be enabled by assigning the `enabled` field a `true` or `false` value.

Passing only the `enabled` field to this endpoint will not alter your current `list` of whitelist entries. However, any modifications to your `list` of entries will overwrite the entire list. For this reason, you must included all existing entries you wish to retain in your `list` in addition to any new entries you intend to add. To remove one or more `list` entries, pass a `list` with only the entries you wish to retain.

You should not add generic domains such as `gmail.com` or `yahoo.com`  in your `list` because your emails will not honor recipients' unsubscribes. This may cause a legal violation of [CAN-SPAM](https://sendgrid.com/docs/glossary/can-spam/) and could damage your sending reputation.

The Address Whitelist setting allows you to specify email addresses or domains for which mail should never be suppressed.

For example, if you own the domain `example.com`, and one or more of your recipients use `email@example.com` addresses, placing `example.com` in the address whitelist setting instructs Twilio SendGrid to ignore all bounces, blocks, and unsubscribes logged for that domain. In other words, all bounces, blocks, and unsubscribes will still be sent to `example.com` as if they were sent under normal sending conditions.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "list": [
    "email1@example.com",
    "example.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-address-whitelist-mail-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Indicates if your email address whitelist is enabled.|
|» list|body|[string]|false|Either a single email address that you want whitelisted or a domain, for which all email addresses belonging to this domain will be whitelisted.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "list": [
    "email1@example.com"
  ]
}
```

## Retrieve bounce purge mail settings

<a id="opIdGET_mail_settings-bounce_purge"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/mail_settings/bounce_purge \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /mail_settings/bounce_purge`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve your current bounce and purge settings.**

The Bounce Perge setting allows you to set a schedule that Twilio SendGrid will use to automatically delete contacts from your soft and hard bounce suppression lists.

A hard bounce occurs when an email message has been returned to the sender because the recipient's address is invalid. A hard bounce might occur because the domain name doesn't exist or because the recipient is unknown.

A soft bounce occurs when an email message reaches the recipient's mail server but is bounced back undelivered before it actually reaches the recipient. A soft bounce might occur because the recipient's inbox is full.

You can also manage this setting in the [Mail Settings section of the Twilio SendGrid App](https://app.sendgrid.com/settings/mail_settings). You can manage your bounces manually using the [Bounces API](https://sendgrid.api-docs.io/v3.0/bounces-api) or the [Bounces menu in the Twilio SendGrid App](https://app.sendgrid.com/suppressions/bounces).

<h3 id="retrieve-bounce-purge-mail-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

> Example responses

  "enabled": false,
  "hard_bounces": 5,
  "soft_bounces": 5
}

## Update bounce purge mail settings

<a id="opIdPATCH_mail_settings-bounce_purge"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/mail_settings/bounce_purge \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": false,
    "hard_bounces": null,
    "soft_bounces": 1234
  }'
```

`PATCH /mail_settings/bounce_purge`

**This endpoint allows you to update your current bounce and purge settings.**

The Bounce Perge setting allows you to set a schedule that Twilio SendGrid will use to automatically delete contacts from your soft and hard bounce suppression lists. The schedule is set in full days by assigning the number of days, an integer, to the `soft_bounces` and/or `hard_bounces` fields.

A hard bounce occurs when an email message has been returned to the sender because the recipient's address is invalid. A hard bounce might occur because the domain name doesn't exist or because the recipient is unknown.

A soft bounce occurs when an email message reaches the recipient's mail server but is bounced back undelivered before it actually reaches the recipient. A soft bounce might occur because the recipient's inbox is full.

You can also manage this setting in the [Mail Settings section of the Twilio SendGrid App](https://app.sendgrid.com/settings/mail_settings). You can manage your bounces manually using the [Bounces API](https://sendgrid.api-docs.io/v3.0/bounces-api) or the [Bounces menu in the Twilio SendGrid App](https://app.sendgrid.com/suppressions/bounces).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": false,
  "hard_bounces": null,
  "soft_bounces": 1234
}
```

<h3 id="update-bounce-purge-mail-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[mail_settings_bounce_purge](#schemamail_settings_bounce_purge)|false|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Indicates if the bounce purge mail setting is enabled.|
|» hard_bounces|body|integer \| null|false|The number of days after which SendGrid will purge all contacts from your hard bounces suppression lists.|
|» soft_bounces|body|integer \| null|false|The number of days after which SendGrid will purge all contacts from your soft bounces suppression lists.|
