```bash
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "",
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /mail_settings/forward_spam`

**This endpoint allows you to update your current Forward Spam mail settings.**

Enabling the Forward Spam setting allows you to specify `email` addresses to which spam reports will be forwarded. You can set multiple addresses by passing this endpoint a comma separated list of emails in a single string.

```
{
  "email": "address1@example.com, address2@exapmle.com",
  "enabled": true
}
```

The Forward Spam setting may also be used to receive emails sent to `abuse@` and `postmaster@` role addresses if you have authenticated your domain.

For example, if you authenticated `example.com` as your root domain and set a custom return path of `sub` for that domain, you could turn on Forward Spam, and any emails sent to `abuse@sub.example.com` or `postmaster@sub.example.com` would be forwarded to the email address you entered in the `email` field.

You can authenticate your domain using the "Authenticate a domain" endpoint or in the [Sender Authentication section of the Twilio SendGrid App](https://app.sendgrid.com/settings/sender_auth). You can also configure the Forward Spam mail settings in the [Mail Settings section of the Twilio SendGrid App](https://app.sendgrid.com/settings/mail_settings).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "",
  "enabled": true
}
```

## Add or Update a Contact

<a id="opIdPUT_mc-contacts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/contacts \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "contacts": [
      {
        "address_line_1": "string",
        "address_line_2": "string",
        "alternate_emails": [
          "string"
        ],
        "city": "string",
        "country": "string",
        "custom_fields": {
          "e2": "Coffee is a beverage that puts one to sleep when not drank.",
          "w1": "2002-10-02T15:00:00Z",
          "w33": 9.5
        },
        "email": "string",
        "first_name": "string",
        "last_name": "string",
        "postal_code": "string",
        "state_province_region": "string"
      }
    ],
    "list_ids": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /marketing/contacts`

**This endpoint allows the [upsert](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/upsert) (insert or update) of up to 30,000 contacts, or 6MB of data, whichever is lower**. 

Because the creation and update of contacts is an asynchronous process, the response will not contain immediate feedback on the processing of your upserted contacts. Rather, it will contain an HTTP 202 response indicating the contacts are queued for processing or an HTTP 4XX error containing validation errors. Should you wish to get the resulting contact's ID or confirm your contacts have been updated or added, you can use the "Get Contacts by Emails" endpoint. 

Please note that custom fields need to have been already created if you wish to set their values for the contacts being upserted. To do this, please use the "Create Custom Field Definition" endpoint.

You will see a `job_id` in the response to your request. This can be used to check the status of your upsert job. To do so, please use the "Import Contacts Status" endpoint.

If the contact already exists in the system, any entries submitted via this endpoint will update the existing contact. The contact to update will be determined only by the `email` field and any fields omitted from the request will remain as they were. A contact's ID cannot be used to update the contact.

The email field will be changed to all lower-case. If a contact is added with an email that exists but contains capital letters, the existing contact with the all lower-case email will be updated.

Twilio SendGrid recommends exporting your contacts regularly as a backup to avoid issues or lost data.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "contacts": [
    {
      "address_line_1": "string",
      "address_line_2": "string",
      "alternate_emails": [
        "string"
      ],
      "city": "string",
      "country": "string",
      "custom_fields": {
        "e2": "Coffee is a beverage that puts one to sleep when not drank.",
        "w1": "2002-10-02T15:00:00Z",
        "w33": 9.5
      },
      "email": "string",
      "first_name": "string",
      "last_name": "string",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "state_province_region": "string"
    }
  ],
  "list_ids": [
    "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-or-update-a-contact-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» contacts|body|[[contact-request](#schemacontact-request)]|true|One or more contacts objects that you intend to upsert. The available fields for a contact, including the required `email` field are described below.|
|» list_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|false|An array of List ID strings that this contact will be added to.|

## Delete Contacts

<a id="opIdDELETE_mc-contacts"></a>

`DELETE /marketing/contacts`

**This endpoint can be used to delete one or more contacts**.

The query parameter `ids` must set to a comma-separated list of contact IDs for bulk contact deletion.

The query parameter `delete_all_contacts` must be set to `"true"` to delete **all** contacts. 

You must set either `ids` or `delete_all_contacts`.

Deletion jobs are processed asynchronously.

Twilio SendGrid recommends exporting your contacts regularly as a backup to avoid issues or lost data.

## Get All Existing Exports

`GET /marketing/contacts/exports`

**Use this endpoint to retrieve details of all current exported jobs**.

It will return an array of objects, each of which records an export job in flight or recently completed. 

Each object's `export_type` field will tell you which kind of export it is and its `status` field will indicate what stage of processing it has reached. Exports which are `ready` will be accompanied by a `urls` field which lists the URLs of the export's downloadable files — there will be more than one if you specified a maximum file size in your initial export request.

Use this endpoint if you have exports in flight but do not know their IDs, which are required for the "Export Contacts Status" endpoint.

Twilio SendGrid recommends exporting your contacts regularly as a backup to avoid issues or lost data.

## Export Contacts

<a id="opIdPOST_mc-contacts-exports"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/contacts/exports \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "file_type": "csv",
    "list_ids": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "max_file_size": 5000,
    "notifications": {
      "email": true
    },
    "segment_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /marketing/contacts/exports`

**Use this endpoint to export lists or segments of contacts**.

If you would just like to have a link to the exported list sent to your email set the `notifications.email` option to `true` in the `POST` payload.

If you would like to download the list, take the `id` that is returned and use the "Export Contacts Status" endpoint to get the `urls`. Once you have the list of URLs, make a `GET` request to each URL provided to download your CSV file(s).

You specify the segements and or/contact lists you wish to export by providing the relevant IDs in, respectively, the `segment_ids` and `list_ids` fields in the request body.

The lists will be provided in either JSON or CSV files. To specify which of these you would required, set the request body `file_type` field to `json` or `csv`.

You can also specify a maximum file size (in MB). If the export file is larger than this, it will be split into multiple files.

Twilio SendGrid recommends exporting your contacts regularly as a backup to avoid issues or lost data.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "file_type": "csv",
  "list_ids": [
    "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  ],
  "max_file_size": 5000,
  "notifications": {
    "email": true
  },
  "segment_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="export-contacts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» file_type|body|string|false|File type for export file. Choose from `json` or `csv`.|
|» list_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|false|IDs of the contact lists you want to export.|
|» max_file_size|body|integer|false|The maximum size of an export file in MB. Note that when this option is specified, multiple output files may be returned from the export.|
|» notifications|body|object|false|none|
|» » email|body|boolean|false|none|
|» segment_ids|body|[string]|false|IDs of the contact segments you want to export.|

|» file_type|json|

## Import Contacts

<a id="opIdPUT_mc-contacts-imports"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/contacts/imports \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "field_mappings": [
      "string"
    ],
    "file_type": "csv",
    "list_ids": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /marketing/contacts/imports`

**This endpoint allows a CSV upload containing up to one million contacts or 5GB of data, whichever is smaller.**

Imports take place asynchronously: the endpoint returns a URL (`upload_uri`) and HTTP headers (`upload_headers`) which can subsequently be used to `PUT` a file of contacts to be  imported into our system.

Uploaded CSV files may also be [gzip-compressed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gzip).

In either case, you must include the field `file_type` with the value `csv` in your request body.

The `field_mappings` paramter is a respective list of field definition IDs to map the uploaded CSV columns to. It allows you to use CSVs where one or more columns are skipped (`null`) or remapped to the contact field. 

For example, if `field_mappings` is set to `[null, "w1", "_rf1"]`, this means skip column 0, map column 1 to the custom field with the ID `w1`, and map column 2 to the reserved field with the ID `_rf1`. See the "Get All Field Definitions" endpoint to fetch your custom and reserved field IDs to use with `field_mappings`.

Once you recieve the response body you can then initiate a **second** API call where you use the supplied URL and HTTP header to upload your file. For example:

`curl --upload-file "file/path.csv" "URL_GIVEN" -H 'HEADER_GIVEN'`

If you'd like to monitor the status of your import job, use the `job_id` and the "Import Contacts Status" endpoint.
Twilio SendGrid recommends exporting your contacts regularly as a backup to avoid issues or lost data.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "field_mappings": [
    "string"
  ],
  "file_type": "csv",
  "list_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="import-contacts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» field_mappings|body|[string \| object \| null]|true|Import file header to reserved/custom field mapping.|

## Import Contacts Status

<a id="opIdGET_marketing-contacts-imports-id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/contacts/imports/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /marketing/contacts/imports/{id}`

**This endpoint can be used to check the status of a contact import job**. 

Use the `job_id` from the "Import Contacts," "Add or Update a Contact," or "Delete Contacts" endpoints as the `id` in the path parameter.

If there is an error with your `PUT` request, download the `errors_url` file and open it to view more details.

The job `status` field indicates whether the job is `pending`, `completed`, `errored`, or `failed`. 

Pending means not started. Completed means finished without any errors. Errored means finished with some errors. Failed means finshed with all errors, or the job was entirely unprocessable: for example, if you attempt to import file format we do not support.

The `results` object will have fields depending on the job type.

Twilio SendGrid recommends exporting your contacts regularly as a backup to avoid issues or lost data.

|id|path|string|true|none|

## Search Contacts

<a id="opIdPOST_mc-contacts-search"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/contacts/search \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "query": "email LIKE '\''ENTER_COMPLETE_OR_PARTIAL_EMAIL_ADDRESS_HERE%'\'' AND CONTAINS(list_ids, '\''YOUR_LIST_IDs'\'')"
  }'
```

`POST /marketing/contacts/search`

**Use this endpoint to locate contacts**.

The request body's `query` field accepts valid [SGQL](https://sendgrid.com/docs/for-developers/sending-email/segmentation-query-language/) for searching for a contact.

Because contact emails are stored in lower case, using SGQL to search by email address requires the provided email address to be in lower case. The SGQL `lower()` function can be used for this.

Only the first 50 contacts that meet the search criteria will be returned.

If the query takes longer than 20 seconds, a `408 Request Timeout` status will be returned.

Formatting the `created_at` and `updated_at` values as Unix timestamps is deprecated. Instead they are returned as ISO format as string.
Twilio SendGrid recommends exporting your contacts regularly as a backup to avoid issues or lost data.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "query": "email LIKE 'ENTER_COMPLETE_OR_PARTIAL_EMAIL_ADDRESS_HERE%' AND CONTAINS(list_ids, 'YOUR_LIST_IDs')"
}
```

## Get Contacts by Emails

<a id="opIdPOST_marketing-contacts-search-emails"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/contacts/search/emails \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "emails": [
      "jane_doe@example.com",
      "john_doe@example.com",
      "joann_doe@example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /marketing/contacts/search/emails`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve up to 100 contacts matching the searched `email` address(es), including any `alternate_emails`.** 

Email addresses are unique to a contact, meaning this endpoint can treat an email address as a primary key to search by. The contact object associated with the address, whether it is their `email` or one of their `alternate_emails` will be returned if matched.

Email addresses in the search request do not need to match the case in which they're stored, but the email addresses in the result will be all lower case. Empty strings are excluded from the search and will not be returned.

This endpoint should be used in place of the "Search Contacts" endpoint when you can provide exact email addresses and do not need to include other [Segmentation Query Language (SGQL)](https://sendgrid.com/docs/for-developers/sending-email/segmentation-query-language/) filters when searching.

If you need to access a large percentage of your contacts, we recommend exporting your contacts with the "Export Contacts" endpoint and filtering the results client side.

This endpoint returns a `200` status code when any contacts match the address(es) you supplied. When searching multiple addresses in a single request, it is possible that some addresses will match a contact while others will not. When a partially successful search like this is made, the matching contacts are returned in an object and an error message is returned for the email address(es) that are not found. 

This endpoint returns a `404` status code when no contacts are found for the provided email address(es).

A `400` status code is returned if any searched addresses are invalid.

Twilio SendGrid recommends exporting your contacts regularly as a backup to avoid issues or lost data.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "emails": [
    "jane_doe@example.com",
    "john_doe@example.com",
    "joann_doe@example.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-contacts-by-emails-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» emails|body|[string]|true|One or more primary emails and/or alternate emails to search through your contacts for.|

> Example responses

## Create Custom Field Definition

<a id="opIdPOST_mc-field_definitions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/field_definitions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "field_type": "Text",
    "name": "custom_field_name"
  }'
```

`POST /marketing/field_definitions`

**This endpoint creates a new custom field definition.**

Custom field definitions are created with the given `name` and `field_type`. Although field names are stored in a case-sensitive manner, all field names must be case-insensitively unique. This means you may create a field named `CamelCase` or `camelcase`, but not both. Additionally, a Custom Field name cannot collide with any Reserved Field names. You should save the returned `id` value in order to update or delete the field at a later date. You can have up to 120 custom fields.

The custom field name should be created using only alphanumeric characters (A-Z and 0-9) and underscores (\_). Custom fields can only begin with letters  A-Z or underscores (_). The field type can be date, text, or number fields. The field type is important for creating segments from your contact database.

**Note: Creating a custom field that begins with a number will cause issues with sending in Marketing Campaigns.**

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "field_type": "Text",
  "name": "custom_field_name"
}
```

<h3 id="create-custom-field-definition-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» field_type|body|string|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» field_type|Text|
|» field_type|Number|
|» field_type|Date|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "_metadata": {
    "self": "https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/marketing/field_definitions/a1_B"
  },
  "field_type": "Text",
  "id": "a1_T",
  "name": "custom_field_name"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "error_id": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "parameter": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-custom-field-definition-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request||Inline|

## Get List of Segments

<a id="opIdGET_marketing-segments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/segments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /marketing/segments`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of segments.**

The query param `parent_list_ids` is treated as a filter.  Any match will be returned.  0 matches will return a response code of 200 with an empty `results` array.

`parent_list_ids` | `no_parent_list_id` | `result`
-----------------:|:--------------------:|:-------------
empty | false | all segments
values | false | segments filtered by list_ids
values | true | segments filtered by list_ids and segments with no parent list_ids
empty | true | segments with no parent list_ids

<h3 id="get-list-of-segments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|parent_list_ids|query|string|false|A comma separated list of list ids to be used when searching for segments with the specified parent_list_id, no more than 50 is allowed|
|no_parent_list_id|query|boolean|false|If set to `true` segments with an empty value of `parent_list_id` will be returned in the filter.  If the value is not present it defaults to 'false'.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "contacts_count": 78434802,
      "created_at": "2921-01-27T19:33:36.479Z",
      "id": "12099613-91e5-4d09-a900-df7626325288",
      "sample_updated_at": "4685-11-26T07:05:04.660Z",
      "updated_at": "2883-07-10T13:13:37.697Z"
    },
    {
      "contacts_count": 34177253,
      "created_at": "2575-07-26T23:17:20.984Z",
      "id": "60c37015-3734-4c8e-b293-68cfa2ae4fa5",
      "name": "amet",
      "parent_list_id": "fd38af3d-3f69-4947-8dca-5fa967e7be82",
      "sample_updated_at": "3074-09-04T09:49:58.127Z",
      "updated_at": "5116-10-15T07:37:40.838Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{

    }
  ]
```

`POST /marketing/segments`

**This endpoint allows you to create a segment.**

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "parent_list_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "query_dsl": "string",
  "parent_list_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
```

<h3 id="create-segment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the segment.|
|» parent_list_ids|body|[string]|false|The array of list ids to filter contacts on when building this segment. It allows only one such list id for now. We will support more in future|

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-segmenting-contacts-v2---beta">Segmenting Contacts V2 - Beta</h1>

## Get List of Segments

<a id="opIdGET_segments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/segments/2.0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /marketing/segments/2.0`

**The Segmentation V2 API is currently in private beta. If you'd like to be added to the beta, please fill out this [form]({https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd5zwC9dRk8lAp1oTWjdGc-aSY69flW_7wnutvKBhpUluSnfQ/viewform)**

The query param `parent_list_ids` is treated as a filter.  Any match will be returned.  0 matches will return a response code of 200 with an empty `results` array.

`parent_list_ids` | `no_parent_list_id` | `result`
-----------------:|:--------------------:|:-------------
empty | false | all segments
values | false | segments filtered by list_ids
values | true | segments filtered by list_ids and segments with no parent list_ids
empty | true | segments with no parent list_ids

<h3 id="get-list-of-segments-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|parent_list_ids|query|string|false|A comma separated list up to 50 in size, to filter segments on.  Only segments that have any of these list ids as the parent list will be retrieved. This is different from the parameter of the same name used when creating a segment.|
|no_parent_list_id|query|boolean|false|If set to `true` segments with an empty value of `parent_list_id` will be returned in the filter.  If the value is not present it defaults to 'false'.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "_metadata": {
    "count": 0,
    "next": "http://example.com",
    "prev": "http://example.com",
    "self": "http://example.com"
  },
  "contacts_count": 0,
  "created_at": "string",
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "name": "string",
  "next_sample_update": "string",
  "parent_list_ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "query_version": "string",
  "sample_updated_at": "string",
  "status": {
    "error_message": "string",
    "query_validation": "string"
  },
  "updated_at": "string"
}
```

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
```

## Create a Sender Identity

<a id="opIdPOST_marketing-senders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/senders \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "1234 Fake St.",
    "address_2": "",
    "city": "San Francisco",
    "country": "United States",
    "from": {
      "email": "orders@example.com",
      "name": "Example Orders"
    },
    "nickname": "Example Orders",
    "reply_to": {
      "email": "support@example.com",
      "name": "Example Support"
    },
    "state": "CA",
    "zip": "94105"
  }'
```

`POST /marketing/senders`

**This endpoint allows you to create a new sender identity.**

*You may create up to 100 unique sender identities.*

Sender identities are required to be verified before use. If your domain has been authenticated, a new sender identity will auto verify on creation. Otherwise an email will be sent to the `from.email`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "1234 Fake St.",
  "address_2": "",
  "city": "San Francisco",
  "country": "United States",
  "from": {
    "email": "orders@example.com",
    "name": "Example Orders"
  },
  "nickname": "Example Orders",
  "reply_to": {
    "email": "support@example.com",
    "name": "Example Support"
  },
  "state": "CA",
  "zip": "94105"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-sender-identity-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» address|body|string|true|The physical address of the sender identity.|
|» address_2|body|string|false|Additional sender identity address information.|
|» city|body|string|true|The city of the sender identity.|
|» country|body|string|true|The country of the sender identity.|
|» from|body|object|true|none|
|» » email|body|string|true|This is where the email will appear to originate from for your recipient|
|» » name|body|string|true|This is the name appended to the from email field. IE - Your name or company name.|
|» nickname|body|string|true|A nickname for the sender identity. Not used for sending.|
|» reply_to|body|object|false|none|
|» » email|body|string|true|This is the email that your recipient will reply to.|
|» » name|body|string|false|This is the name appended to the reply to email field. IE - Your name or company name.|
|» state|body|string|false|The state of the sender identity.|
|» zip|body|string|false|The zipcode of the sender identity.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "address": "123 Elm St.",
  "address_2": "Apt. 456",
  "city": "Denver",
  "country": "United States",
  "created_at": 1449872165,
  "from": {
    "email": "from@example.com",
    "name": "Example INC"
  },
  "id": 1,
  "locked": false,
  "nickname": "My Sender ID",
  "reply_to": {
    "email": "replyto@example.com",
    "name": "Example INC"
  },
  "state": "Colorado",
  "updated_at": 1449872165,
  "verified": true,
  "zip": "80202"
}
```

```json
    {

    }
  ]
```

## Create Single Send

<a id="opIdPOST_marketing-singlesends"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/singlesends \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "categories": [
      "string"
    ],
    "email_config": {
      "custom_unsubscribe_url": "http://example.com",
      "design_id": "string",
      "editor": "code",
      "generate_plain_content": true,
      "html_content": "string",
      "ip_pool": "string",
      "plain_content": "string",
      "sender_id": 0,
      "subject": "string",
      "suppression_group_id": 0
    },
    "name": "string",
    "send_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "send_to": {
      "all": false,
      "list_ids": [
        "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
      ],
      "segment_ids": [
        "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /marketing/singlesends`

**This endpoint allows you to create a new Single Send.**

Please note that if you are migrating from the previous version of Single Sends, you no longer need to pass a template ID with your request to this endpoint. Instead, you will pass all template data in the `email_config` object.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "categories": [
    "string"
  ],
  "email_config": {
    "custom_unsubscribe_url": "http://example.com",
    "design_id": "string",
    "editor": "code",
    "generate_plain_content": true,
    "html_content": "string",
    "ip_pool": "string",
    "plain_content": "string",
    "sender_id": 0,
    "subject": "string",
    "suppression_group_id": 0
  },
  "name": "string",
  "send_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "send_to": {
    "all": false,
    "list_ids": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "segment_ids": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-single-send-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[singlesend_request](#schemasinglesend_request)|false|none|
|» categories|body|[string]|false|The categories to associate with this Single Send.|
|» email_config|body|object|false|none|
|» » custom_unsubscribe_url|body|string(uri) \| null|false|The URL allowing recipients to unsubscribe — you must provide this or the `suppression_group_id`.|
|» » design_id|body|string|false|A `design_id` can be used in place of `html_content`, `plain_content`, and/or `subject`. You can retrieve a design's ID from the ["List Designs" endpoint](https://sendgrid.api-docs.io/v3.0/designs-api/list-designs) or by pulling it from the design's detail page URL in the Marketing Campaigns App.|
|» » editor|body|string|false|The editor — `"design"` or `"code"` — used to modify the Single Send's design in the Marketing Campaigns App.|
|» » generate_plain_content|body|boolean|false|If set to `true`, `plain_content` is always generated from `html_content`. If set to false, `plain_content` is not altered.|
|» » html_content|body|string|false|The HTML content of the Single Send. Do not include this field when using a `design_id`.|
|» » ip_pool|body|string \| null|false|The name of the IP Pool from which the Single Send emails are sent.|
|» » plain_content|body|string|false|The plain text content of the Single Send. Do not include this field when using a `design_id`.|
|» » sender_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the verified Sender. You can retrieve a verified Sender's ID from the ["Get Verified Senders" endpoint](https://sendgrid.api-docs.io/v3.0/sender-verification/get-verified-senders) or by pulling it from the Sender's detail page URL in the SendGrid App.|
|» » subject|body|string|false|The subject line of the Single Send. Do not include this field when using a `design_id`.|
|» » suppression_group_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the Suppression Group to allow recipients to unsubscribe — you must provide this or the `custom_unsubscribe_url`.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the Single Send.|
|» send_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The ISO 8601 time at which to send the Single Send — this must be set for a future time.|
|» send_to|body|object|false|none|
|» » all|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to send to All Contacts. If set to `false`, at least one `list_ids` or `segment_ids` value must be provided before the Single Send is scheduled to be sent to recipients.|
|» » list_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|false|The recipient List IDs that will receive the Single Send.|
|» » segment_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|false|The recipient Segment IDs that will receive the Single Send.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » editor|code|
|» » editor|design|

## Get Single Sends Search

<a id="opIdPOST_marketing-singlesends-search"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/singlesends/search \
  -X POST \
```

`POST /marketing/singlesends/search`

**This endpoint allows you to search for Single Sends based on specified criteria.**

You can search for Single Sends by passing a combination of values using the `name`, `status`, and `categories` request body fields.

For example, if you want to search for all Single Sends that are "drafts" or "scheduled" and also associated with the category "shoes," your request body may look like the example below.

```javascript
{
  "status": [
    "draft",
    "scheduled"
  ],
  "categories": [
    "shoes"
  ],
}
```

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "categories": [
    "string"
  ],
  "name": "string",
  "status": [
    "draft"
  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_size|query|integer|false|none|
|page_token|query|string|false|none|
|body|body|[singlesend_search](#schemasinglesend_search)|false|none|
|» categories|body|[string]|false|categories to associate with this Single Send, match any single send that has at least one of the categories|
|» name|body|string|false|leading and trailing wildcard search on name of the Single Send|
|» status|body|[string]|false|current status of the Single Send|

## Duplicate Single Send

<a id="opIdPOST_marketing-singlesends-id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/singlesends/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /marketing/singlesends/{id}`

**This endpoint allows you to duplicate an existing Single Send using its Single Send ID.**

Duplicating a Single Send is useful when you want to create a Single Send but don't want to start from scratch. Once duplicated, you can update or edit the Single Send by making a PATCH request to the `/marketing/singlesends/{id}` endpoint.
 
If you leave the `name` field blank, your duplicate will be assigned the name of the Single Send it was copied from with the text “Copy of ” prepended to it. The `name` field length is limited to 100 characters, so the end of the new Single Send name, including “Copy of ”, will be trimmed if the name exceeds this limit.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="duplicate-single-send-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the duplicate Single Send. If you choose to leave the name field blank, your duplicate will be assigned the name of the Single Send it was copied from with the text 'Copy of ' prepended to it. The end of the new Single Send name, including 'Copy of ', will be trimmed if the name exceeds the character limit.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "categories": [
    "unique opens"
  ],
  "created_at": "2020-05-18T17:28:27.272Z",

    "ip_pool": null,
    "plain_content": "",
    "sender_id": null,
    "subject": "",
    "suppression_group_id": null
  },

  "name": "Example API Created Single Send",
  "send_at": "2020-06-16T00:19:55.106Z",
  "send_to": {
    "list_ids": [
      "f2fe66a1-43f3-4e3a-87b1-c6a600d805f0"
    ]
  },
  "status": "scheduled"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
      "error_id": "string",

      "message": "string"
    }
```

```bash
        "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /marketing/singlesends/{id}`

**This endpoint allows you to update a Single Send using a Single Send ID.**

You only need to pass the fields you want to update. Any blank/missing fields will remain unaltered.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "categories": [
    "string"
  ],
  "email_config": {
    "custom_unsubscribe_url": "http://example.com",
    "design_id": "string",
    "editor": "code",
    "generate_plain_content": true,
    "html_content": "string",
    "ip_pool": "string",
    "plain_content": "string",
    "sender_id": 0,
    "subject": "string",
    "suppression_group_id": 0
  },
  "name": "string",
  "send_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "send_to": {
    "all": false,
    "list_ids": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "segment_ids": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-single-send-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[singlesend_request](#schemasinglesend_request)|false|none|
|» categories|body|[string]|false|The categories to associate with this Single Send.|
|» email_config|body|object|false|none|
|» » custom_unsubscribe_url|body|string(uri) \| null|false|The URL allowing recipients to unsubscribe — you must provide this or the `suppression_group_id`.|
|» » design_id|body|string|false|A `design_id` can be used in place of `html_content`, `plain_content`, and/or `subject`. You can retrieve a design's ID from the ["List Designs" endpoint](https://sendgrid.api-docs.io/v3.0/designs-api/list-designs) or by pulling it from the design's detail page URL in the Marketing Campaigns App.|
|» » editor|body|string|false|The editor — `"design"` or `"code"` — used to modify the Single Send's design in the Marketing Campaigns App.|
|» » generate_plain_content|body|boolean|false|If set to `true`, `plain_content` is always generated from `html_content`. If set to false, `plain_content` is not altered.|
|» » html_content|body|string|false|The HTML content of the Single Send. Do not include this field when using a `design_id`.|
|» » ip_pool|body|string \| null|false|The name of the IP Pool from which the Single Send emails are sent.|
|» » plain_content|body|string|false|The plain text content of the Single Send. Do not include this field when using a `design_id`.|
|» » sender_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the verified Sender. You can retrieve a verified Sender's ID from the ["Get Verified Senders" endpoint](https://sendgrid.api-docs.io/v3.0/sender-verification/get-verified-senders) or by pulling it from the Sender's detail page URL in the SendGrid App.|
|» » subject|body|string|false|The subject line of the Single Send. Do not include this field when using a `design_id`.|
|» » suppression_group_id|body|integer \| null|false|The ID of the Suppression Group to allow recipients to unsubscribe — you must provide this or the `custom_unsubscribe_url`.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the Single Send.|
|» send_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The ISO 8601 time at which to send the Single Send — this must be set for a future time.|
|» send_to|body|object|false|none|
|» » all|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to send to All Contacts. If set to `false`, at least one `list_ids` or `segment_ids` value must be provided before the Single Send is scheduled to be sent to recipients.|
|» » list_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|false|The recipient List IDs that will receive the Single Send.|
|» » segment_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|false|The recipient Segment IDs that will receive the Single Send.|

|» » editor|design|

## Schedule Single Send

<a id="opIdPUT_marketing-singlesends-id-schedule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/singlesends/string/schedule \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "send_at": "3752-01-28T23:21:52.575Z"
  }'
```

`PUT /marketing/singlesends/{id}/schedule`

**This endpoint allows you to schedule a Single Send for future delivery using a Single Send ID.**

To schedule a Single Send, you must pass a date string in ISO 8601 time format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ)  using the required `send_at` field. For example, the ISO 8601 format for 9:00 AM UTC on May 6, 2020 would be `2020-05-06T09:00:00Z`. You may also pass the string `"now"` to send the Single Send immediately.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "send_at": "3752-01-28T23:21:52.575Z"
}
```

<h3 id="schedule-single-send-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» send_at|body|string(date-time)|true|This is the ISO 8601 time at which to send the Single Send; must be in future, or the string "now"|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» send_at|now|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "send_at": "3752-01-28T23:21:52.575Z",
  "status": "scheduled"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "error_id": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "error_id": "string",
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|404|Not Found||Inline|

`DELETE /marketing/singlesends/{id}/schedule`

**This endpoint allows you to cancel a scheduled Single Send using a Single Send ID.**

Making a DELETE request to this endpoint will cancel the scheduled sending of a Single Send. The request will not delete the Single Send itself. Deleting a Single Send can be done by passing a DELETE request to `/marketing/singlesends/{id}`.

## Get All Automation Stats

<a id="opIdgetall-automation-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/stats/automations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /marketing/stats/automations`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve stats for all your Automations.**

By default, all of your Automations will be returned, but you can specify a selection by passing in a comma-separated list of Automation IDs as the value of the query string parameter `automation_ids`.

Responses are paginated. You can limit the number of responses returned per batch using the `page_size` query string parameter. The default is 50, but you specify a value between 1 and 100.

You can retrieve a specific page of responses with the `page_token` query string parameter.

<h3 id="get-all-automation-stats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|automation_ids|query|[string]|false|This endpoint returns all automation IDs if no `automation_ids` are specified.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|The number of elements you want returned on each page.|
|page_token|query|string|false|The stats endpoints are paginated. To get the next page, call the passed `_metadata.next` URL. If `_metadata.prev` doesn't exist, you're at the first page. Similarly, if `_metadata.next` is not present, you're at the last page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "_metadata": {
    "count": 0,
    "next": "http://example.com",
    "prev": "http://example.com",
    "self": "http://example.com"
  },
  "results": [
    {
      "aggregation": "total",
      "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "stats": {
        "bounce_drops": 0,
        "bounces": 0,
        "clicks": 0,
        "delivered": 0,
        "invalid_emails": 0,
        "opens": 0,
        "requests": 0,
        "spam_report_drops": 0,
        "spam_reports": 0,
        "unique_clicks": 0,
        "unique_opens": 0,
        "unsubscribes": 0
      },
      "step_id": "all"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-all-automation-stats-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[automations-response](#schemaautomations-response)|
|400|Bad Request||[global_error_response_schema](#schemaglobal_error_response_schema)|

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`GET /marketing/stats/automations/export`

**This endpoint allows you to export Automation stats as CSV data**.

You can specify one Automation or many: include as many Automation IDs as you need, separating them with commas, as the value of the `ids` query string paramter.

The data is returned as plain text response but in CSV format, so your application making the call can present the information in whatever way is most appropriate, or just save the data as a `.csv` file.

<h3 id="export-automation-stats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|[string]|false|The IDs of Automations for which to export stats.|
|timezone|query|string|false|The [IANA Area/Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database#Names_of_time_zones) string representing the timezone in which the stats are to be presented; i.e. `"America/Chicago"`. This parameter changes the timezone format only; it does not alter which stats are returned.|

```json
"string"
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Get Automation Stats by ID

<a id="opIdget-automation-stat"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/stats/automations/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /marketing/stats/automations/{id}`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve stats for a single Automation using its ID.**

Multiple Automation IDs can be retrieved using the "Get All Automation Stats" endpoint. Once you have an ID, this endpoint will return detailed stats for the single automation specified.

You may constrain the stats returned using the `start_date` and `end_date` query string parameters. You can also use the `group_by` and `aggregated_by` query string parameters to further refine the stats returned.

<h3 id="get-automation-stats-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|group_by|query|[string]|false|Automations can have multiple steps. Including `step_id` as a `group_by` metric allows further granularity of stats.|
|step_ids|query|[string(uuid)]|false|Comma-separated list of `step_ids` that you want the link stats for.|
|aggregated_by|query|string|false|Dictates how the stats are time-sliced. Currently, `"total"` and `"day"` are supported.|
|start_date|query|string(date)|false|Format: `YYYY-MM-DD`. If this parameter is included, the stats' start date is included in the search.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|false|Format: `YYYY-MM-DD`.If this parameter is included, the stats' end date is included in the search.|
|timezone|query|string|false|[IANA Area/Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database#Names_of_time_zones) string representing the timezone in which the stats are to be presented, e.g., "America/Chicago".|
|page_size|query|integer|false|The number of elements you want returned on each page.|
|page_token|query|string|false|The stats endpoints are paginated. To get the next page, call the passed `_metadata.next` URL. If `_metadata.prev` doesn't exist, you're at the first page. Similarly, if `_metadata.next` is not present, you're at the last page.|
|id|path|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|group_by|step_id|
|aggregated_by|day|
|aggregated_by|total|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "_metadata": {
    "count": 0,
    "next": "http://example.com",
    "prev": "http://example.com",
    "self": "http://example.com"
  },
  "results": [
    {
      "aggregation": "total",
      "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "stats": {
        "bounce_drops": 0,
        "bounces": 0,
        "clicks": 0,
        "delivered": 0,
        "invalid_emails": 0,
        "opens": 0,
        "requests": 0,
        "spam_report_drops": 0,
        "spam_reports": 0,
        "unique_clicks": 0,
        "unique_opens": 0,
        "unsubscribes": 0
      },
      "step_id": "all"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-automation-stats-by-id-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|200|OK||[automations-response](#schemaautomations-response)|

## Export Single Send Stats

<a id="opIdget-singlesend-stats-export"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/stats/singlesends/export \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /marketing/stats/singlesends/export`

**This endpoint allows you to export Single Send stats as .CSV data**.

You can specify one Single Send or many: include as many Single Send IDs as you need, separating them with commas, as the value of the `ids` query string paramter.

The data is returned as plain text response but in .CSV format, so your application making the call can present the information in whatever way is most appropriate, or just save the data as a .csv file.

<h3 id="export-single-send-stats-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ids|query|[string]|false|The IDs of Single Sends for which to export stats.|
|timezone|query|string|false|The [IANA Area/Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database#Names_of_time_zones) string representing the timezone in which the stats are to be presented; i.e. `"America/Chicago"`. This parameter changes the timezone format only; it does not alter which stats are returned.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
"string"
```

## Get Single Send Stats by ID

<a id="opIdget-singlesend-stat"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/stats/singlesends/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /marketing/stats/singlesends/{id}`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve stats for an individual Single Send using a Single Send ID.**

Multiple Single Send IDs can be retrieved using the "Get All Single Sends Stats" endpoint. Once you have an ID, this endpoint will return detailed stats for the Single Send specified.

You may constrain the stats returned using the `start_date` and `end_date` query string parameters. You can also use the `group_by` and `aggregated_by` query string parameters to further refine the stats returned.

<h3 id="get-single-send-stats-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregated_by|query|string|false|Dictates how the stats are time-sliced. Currently, `"total"` and `"day"` are supported.|
|start_date|query|string(date)|false|Format: `YYYY-MM-DD`. If this parameter is included, the stats' start date is included in the search.|
|end_date|query|string(date)|false|Format: `YYYY-MM-DD`.If this parameter is included, the stats' end date is included in the search.|
|timezone|query|string|false|[IANA Area/Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database#Names_of_time_zones) string representing the timezone in which the stats are to be presented, e.g., "America/Chicago".|
|page_size|query|integer|false|The number of elements you want returned on each page.|
|page_token|query|string|false|The stats endpoints are paginated. To get the next page, call the passed `_metadata.next` URL. If `_metadata.prev` doesn't exist, you're at the first page. Similarly, if `_metadata.next` is not present, you're at the last page.|
|group_by|query|[string]|false|A/B Single Sends have multiple variation IDs and phase IDs. Including these additional fields allows further granularity of stats by these fields.|
|id|path|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|aggregated_by|day|
|aggregated_by|total|
|group_by|ab_variation|
|group_by|ab_phase|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "_metadata": {
    "count": 0,
    "next": "http://example.com",
    "prev": "http://example.com",
    "self": "http://example.com"
  },
  "results": [
    {
      "ab_phase": "all",
      "ab_variation": "all",
      "aggregation": "total",
      "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "stats": {
        "bounce_drops": 0,
        "bounces": 0,
        "clicks": 0,
        "delivered": 0,
        "invalid_emails": 0,
        "opens": 0,
        "requests": 0,
        "spam_report_drops": 0,
        "spam_reports": 0,
        "unique_clicks": 0,
        "unique_opens": 0,
        "unsubscribes": 0
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Get Single Send Click Tracking Stats by ID

<a id="opIdget-singlesend-link-stat"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/stats/singlesends/string/links \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /marketing/stats/singlesends/{id}/links`

**This endpoint lets you retrieve click-tracking stats for one Single Send**.

The stats returned list the URLs embedded in the specified Single Send and the number of clicks each one received.

Responses are paginated. You can limit the number of responses returned per batch using the `page_size` query string parameter. The default is 50, but you specify a value between 1 and 100.

You can retrieve a specific page of responses with the `page_token` query string parameter.

<h3 id="get-single-send-click-tracking-stats-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_size|query|integer|false|The number of elements you want returned on each page.|
|page_token|query|string|false|The stats endpoints are paginated. To get the next page, call the passed `_metadata.next` URL. If `_metadata.prev` doesn't exist, you're at the first page. Similarly, if `_metadata.next` is not present, you're at the last page.|
|group_by|query|[string]|false|A/B Single Sends have multiple variation IDs and phase IDs. Including these additional fields allows further granularity of stats by these fields.|
|ab_variation_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|ab_phase_id|query|string|false|none|
|id|path|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|group_by|ab_variation|
|group_by|ab_phase|
|ab_phase_id|test|
|ab_phase_id|send|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "_metadata": {
    "count": 0,
    "next": "http://example.com",
    "prev": "http://example.com",
    "self": "http://example.com"
  },
  "results": [
    {
      "ab_phase": "send",
      "ab_variation": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "clicks": 1,
      "url": "http://example.com",
      "url_location": 0
    }
  ],
  "total_clicks": 0
}
```

```json
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}

```

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-send-test-email">Send Test Email</h1>

## Send a Test Marketing Email

<a id="opIdPOST_marketing-test-send_email"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/marketing/test/send_email \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "custom_unsubscribe_url": "https://example.com/unsubscribe",
    "emails": [
      "janedoe@example.com",
      "tiramisu@example.com",
      "bundt@example.com"
    ],
    "sender_id": 6060664,
    "suppression_group_id": 21865513,
    "template_id": "f8f77db8-b9fa-4b3c-9ee8-de3d582016b8",
    "version_id_override": "7734f757-8eb8-4d22-b7f0-779a72f32986"
  }'
```

`POST /marketing/test/send_email`

**This endpoint allows you to send a test marketing email to a list of email addresses**.

Before sending a marketing message, you can test it using this endpoint. You may specify up to **10 contacts** in the `emails` request body field. You must also specify a `template_id` and include either a `from_address` or `sender_id`. You can manage your templates with the [Twilio SendGrid App](https://mc.sendgrid.com/dynamic-templates) or the [Transactional Templates API](https://sendgrid.api-docs.io/v3.0/transactional-templates).

> Please note that this endpoint works with Dynamic Transactional Templates only. Legacy Transactional Templates will not be delivered.

For more information about managing Dynamic Transactional Templates, see [How to Send Email with Dynamic Transactional Templates](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/sending-email/how-to-send-an-email-with-dynamic-transactional-templates/).

You can also test your Single Sends in the [Twilio SendGrid Marketing Campaigns UI](https://mc.sendgrid.com/single-sends).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_unsubscribe_url": "https://example.com/unsubscribe",
  "emails": [
    "janedoe@example.com",
    "tiramisu@example.com",
    "bundt@example.com"
  ],
  "sender_id": 6060664,
  "suppression_group_id": 21865513,
  "template_id": "f8f77db8-b9fa-4b3c-9ee8-de3d582016b8",
  "version_id_override": "7734f757-8eb8-4d22-b7f0-779a72f32986"
}
```

<h3 id="send-a-test-marketing-email-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» custom_unsubscribe_url|body|string|false|A custom unsubscribe URL.|
|» emails|body|[string(email)]|true|An array of email addresses you want to send the test message to.|
|» from_address|body|string(email)|false|You can either specify this address or specify a verified sender ID.|
|» sender_id|body|integer|false|This ID must belong to a verified sender. Alternatively, you may supply a `from_address` email.|
|» suppression_group_id|body|integer|false|none|
|» template_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the template that you would like to use. If you use a template that contains a subject and content (either text or HTML), then those values specified at the personalizations or message level will not be used.|
|» version_id_override|body|string(uuid)|false| You can override the active template with an alternative template version by passing the version ID in this field. If this field is blank, the active template version will be used.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-query">Query</h1>

## Filter all messages

<a id="opIdGET-messages"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/messages?query=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /messages`

This is **BETA** functionality. You may not have access, and we reserve the right to change functionality without notice.

Filter all messages to search your Email Activity. All queries need to be [URL encoded](https://meyerweb.com/eric/tools/dencoder/), and have this format:

`query={query_type}="{query_content}"`

encoded, this would look like this:

`query=type%3D%22query_content%22`

for example:

Filter by a specific email - `query=to_email%3D%22example%40example.com%22`

Filter by subject line - `query=subject%3d%22A%20Great%20Subject%22`

**Full list of basic query types and examples:**


| **Filter query**    | **Unencoded Example** (put this one into the try it out query - it'll automatically encode it for you) | **Encoded Example** (use this one in your code)                        |
|-----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| msg_id          | msg_id=“filter0307p1las1-16816-5A023E36-1.0”                                                                               | msg_id%3D%22filter0307p1las1-16816-5A023E36-1.0%22           |
| from_email      | from_email=“testing@sendgrid.net”                                                                                          | from_email%3D%22testing%40sendgrid.net%22                    |
| subject         | subject="This is a subject test"                                                                                      | subject%22This%20is%20a%20subject%20test%22                  |
| to_email        | to_email="example@example.com"                                                                                       | to_email%3D%22example%40example.com%22                       |
| status          |                                                                                                                            | status%22processed%22                                        |
| template_id     |                                                                                                                            |                                                                    |
| asm_group_id    |                                                                                                                            |                                                                    |
| api_key_id      |                                                                                                                            |                                                                    |
| events          | status="processed"                                                                                                   | status%3D%22processed%22                                     |
| originating_ip  |                                                                                                                            |                                                                    |
| categories      |                                                                                                                            |                                                                    |
| unique_args     |                                                                                                                            |                                                                    |
| outbound_ip     |                                                                                                                            |                                                                    |
| last_event_time | last_event_time=“2017-11-07T23:13:58Z”                                                                               | last_event_time%3D%E2%80%9C2017-11-07T23%3A13%3A58Z%E2%80%9D |
| clicks          | clicks="0"                                                                                                           | clicks%3D%220%22                                             |

For information about building compound queries, and for the full query language functionality, see the [query language reference](https://docs.google.com/a/sendgrid.com/document/d/1fWoKTFNfg5UUsB6t9KuIcSo9CetKF_T0bGfWJ_gdPCs/edit?usp=sharing).

Coming soon, example compound queries: limit + to email + date

<h3 id="filter-all-messages-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|true|Use the query syntax  to filter your email activity.|
|limit|query|number|false|The number of messages returned. This parameter must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 1000|
|X-Query-Id|header|string|false|none|
|X-Cursor|header|string|false|none|
|Authorization|header|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "messages": [
    {
      "clicks_count": 0,
      "from_email": "from@test.com",
      "last_event_time": 1495064728,
      "last_timestamp": 1495064728,
      "msg_id": "abc123",
      "opens_count": 0,

      "subject": "something profound",
      "to_email": "to@test.com"
    },
    {

    },
    {
```

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-csv-ui-only">CSV (UI only)</h1>

## Request CSV

<a id="opIdPOST_v3-messages-download"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/messages/download \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /messages/download`

This is BETA functionality. You may not have access, and we reserve the right to change functionality without notice.

This request will kick off a backend process to generate a CSV file. Once generated, the worker will then send an email for the user download the file. The link will expire in 3 days.

The CSV fill contain the last 1 million messages. This endpoint will be rate limited to 1 request every 12 hours (rate limit may change).

This endpoint is similar to the GET Single Message endpoint - the only difference is that /download is added to indicate that this is a CSV download requests but the same query is used to determine what the CSV should contain.

<h3 id="request-csv-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|Uses a SQL like syntax to indicate which messages to include in the CSV|
|Authorization|header|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "message": "An email will be sent to jane_doe@example.com when the CSV is ready to download.",
  "status": "pending"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "some error"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "",
      "message": "too many requests"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "internal server error"
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted||Inline|
|400|Bad Request||Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests||Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error||Inline|

## Download CSV

<a id="opIdGET_v3-messages-download-download_uuid"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/messages/download/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /messages/download/{download_uuid}`

**This endpoint will return a presigned URL that can be used to download the CSV that was requested from the "Request a CSV" endpoint.**

<h3 id="download-csv-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Authorization|header|string|true|none|
|download_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|UUID used to locate the download csv request entry in the DB.<br><br>This is the UUID provided in the email sent to the user when their csv file is ready to download|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "csv": "https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/sendgrid-rts-development-queries/013c31af-7c9a-49e6-922c-d990f4aff151.csv?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-Credential=AKIAI4NOW7APZHRFYGWQ%2F20170728%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Date=20170728T223936Z&X-Amz-Signature=5c13ede58b211799ab1a556280bd316c404eac3aef1450c47906a077166c4ab4",
  "presigned_url": "https://example.com"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "",
      "message": "download token is invalid or expired"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "internal server error"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-settings---partner">Settings - Partner</h1>

## Returns a list of all partner settings.

<a id="opIdGET_partner_settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/partner_settings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /partner_settings`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of all partner settings that you can enable.**

Our partner settings allow you to integrate your SendGrid account with our partners to increase your SendGrid experience and functionality. For more information about our partners, and how you can begin integrating with them, please visit our [Partners documentation](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/partners/).

<h3 id="returns-a-list-of-all-partner-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of settings to return per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The paging offset.|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": [
    {
      "description": "A description of a partner.",
      "enabled": true,
      "name": "partner_name",
      "title": "Partner title"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="returns-a-list-of-all-partner-settings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="returns-a-list-of-all-partner-settings-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|result|[object]|false|none|none|
|» description|string|true|none|A description of this partner setting.|
|» enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicates if this partner setting has been enabled.|
|» name|string|true|none|The name of the partner setting.|
|» title|string|true|none|The title of the partner.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization
</aside>

## Returns all New Relic partner settings.

<a id="opIdGET_partner_settings-new_relic"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/partner_settings/new_relic \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /partner_settings/new_relic`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve your current New Relic partner settings.**

Our partner settings allow you to integrate your SendGrid account with our partners to increase your SendGrid experience and functionality. For more information about our partners, and how you can begin integrating with them, please visit our [Partners documentation](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/partners/).

By integrating with New Relic, you can send your SendGrid email statistics to your New Relic Dashboard. If you enable this setting, your stats will be sent to New Relic every 5 minutes. You will need your New Relic License Key to enable this setting. For more information, please see our [SendGrid for New Relic documentation](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/analytics-and-reporting/tracking-stats-using-new-relic/).

<h3 id="returns-all-new-relic-partner-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "enable_subuser_statistics": false,
  "enabled": true,
  "license_key": ""
}
```

<h3 id="returns-all-new-relic-partner-settings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[partner_settings_new_relic](#schemapartner_settings_new_relic)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization
</aside>

## Updates New Relic partner settings.

<a id="opIdPATCH_partner_settings-new_relic"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/partner_settings/new_relic \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "enable_subuser_statistics": true,
    "enabled": true,
    "license_key": ""
  }'
```

`PATCH /partner_settings/new_relic`

**This endpoint allows you to update or change your New Relic partner settings.**

Our partner settings allow you to integrate your SendGrid account with our partners to increase your SendGrid experience and functionality. For more information about our partners, and how you can begin integrating with them, please visit our [Partners documentation](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/partners/).

By integrating with New Relic, you can send your SendGrid email statistics to your New Relic Dashboard. If you enable this setting, your stats will be sent to New Relic every 5 minutes. You will need your New Relic License Key to enable this setting. For more information, please see our [SendGrid for New Relic documentation](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/analytics-and-reporting/tracking-stats-using-new-relic/).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enable_subuser_statistics": true,
  "enabled": true,
  "license_key": ""
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|

|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Indicates if this partner setting is enabled.|
|» license_key|body|string|false|The license key for your New Relic account.|

> Example responses

```json
  "enable_subuser_statistics": true,
  "enabled": true,
  "license_key": ""
```

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-api-key-permissions">API Key Permissions</h1>

## Retrieve a list of scopes for which this user has access.

<a id="opIdGET_scopes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/scopes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /scopes`

**This endpoint returns a list of all scopes that this user has access to.**

API Keys are used to authenticate with [SendGrid's v3 API](https://sendgrid.api-docs.io/v3.0/how-to-use-the-sendgrid-v3-api/api-authorization).

API Keys may be assigned certain permissions, or scopes, that limit which API endpoints they are able to access.

This endpoint returns all the scopes assigned to the key you use to authenticate with it. To retrieve the scopes assigned to another key, you can pass an API key ID to the "Retrieve an existing API key" endpoint.

For a more detailed explanation of how you can use API Key permissions, please visit our [API Keys documentation](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/api-keys/).

<h3 id="retrieve-a-list-of-scopes-for-which-this-user-has-access-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "scopes": [
    "mail.send",
    "alerts.create",
    "alerts.read"
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": null,
      "message": "authorization required"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-list-of-scopes-for-which-this-user-has-access-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|401|Unauthorized||Inline|
|403|Forbidden||[global_error_response_schema](#schemaglobal_error_response_schema)|
|404|Not Found||[global_error_response_schema](#schemaglobal_error_response_schema)|
|500|Internal Server Error||Inline|

<h3 id="retrieve-a-list-of-scopes-for-which-this-user-has-access-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scopes|[string]|true|none|The list of scopes for which this user has access.|

Status Code **401**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[object]|true|none|This 401 response indicates that the user making the call doesn't have the authorization to view the list of scopes.|
|» field|object \| null|false|none|This empty field is returned instead of the list of scopes if the user making the call doesn't have the authorization required.|
|» message|string|true|none|Explains why the scopes cannot be returned.|

Status Code **500**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[object]|false|none|none|
|» message|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization
</aside>

## Invite teammate

<a id="opIdPOST_v3-teammates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/teammates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "teammate1@example.com",
    "is_admin": false,
    "scopes": [
      "user.profile.read",
      "user.profile.update"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /teammates`

**This endpoint allows you to invite a Teammate to your account via email.**

You can set a Teammate's initial permissions using the `scopes` array in the request body. Teammate's will receive a minimum set of scopes from Twilio SendGrid that are necessary for the Teammate to function.

**Note:** A teammate invite will expire after 7 days, but you may resend the invitation at any time to reset the expiration date.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "teammate1@example.com",
  "is_admin": false,
  "scopes": [
    "user.profile.read",
    "user.profile.update"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="invite-teammate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» email|body|string|true|New teammate's email|
|» is_admin|body|boolean|true|Set to true if teammate should be an admin user|
|» scopes|body|[string]|true|Set to specify list of scopes that teammate should have. Should be empty if teammate is an admin.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "email": "teammate1@example.com",
  "is_admin": false,
  "scopes": [
    "user.profile.read",
    "user.profile.update"
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "string",
      "message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="invite-teammate-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request||Inline|

<h3 id="invite-teammate-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|email|string|false|none|Teammate's email address|
|is_admin|boolean|false|none|Set to true if teammate should have admin privileges|
|scopes|[object]|false|none|Initial set of permissions to give to teammate if they accept the invite|
|token|string|false|none|Token to identify invite|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[object]|false|none|none|
|» field|string|false|none|none|
|» message|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization
</aside>

<a id="opIdGET_v3-teammates-pending"></a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /teammates/pending`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of all pending Teammate invitations.**

Each teammate invitation is valid for 7 days. Users may resend the invitation to refresh the expiration date.

<h3 id="retrieve-all-pending-teammates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

```json
{
  "result": [
    {
      "email": "user1@example.com",
      "expiration_date": 1456424263,
      "is_admin": false,
      "pending_id": "abcd123abc",
      "scopes": [
        "user.profile.read",
        "user.profile.edit"
      ]
    },
    {
      "email": "user2@example.com",
      "expiration_date": 1456424263,
      "is_admin": true,
      "pending_id": "bcde234bcd",
      "scopes": []
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-all-pending-teammates-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|result|[object]|false|none|none|
|» email|string|false|none|Email address teammate invite will be sent to|
|» expiration_date|integer|false|none|timestamp indicates when invite will expire. Expiration is 7 days after invite creation|
|» is_admin|boolean|false|none|Set to true to indicate teammate should have the same set of permissions as parent user|
|» scopes|[string]|false|none|List of permissions to give teammate if they accept|
|» token|string|false|none|Invitation token used to identify user|
