## Update teammate's permissions

<a id="opIdPATCH_v3-teammates-username"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/teammates/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "is_admin": false,
    "scopes": [
      "user.profile.read",
      "user.profile.edit"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /teammates/{username}`

**This endpoint allows you to update a teammate’s permissions.**

To turn a teammate into an admin, the request body should contain an `is_admin` set to `true`. Otherwise, set `is_admin` to `false` and pass in all the scopes that a teammate should have.

**Only the parent user or other admin teammates can update another teammate’s permissions.**

**Admin users can only update permissions.**

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "is_admin": false,
  "scopes": [
    "user.profile.read",
    "user.profile.edit"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-teammates-permissions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|username|path|string|true|The username of the teammate that you want to retrieve.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» is_admin|body|boolean|true|Set to True if this teammate should be promoted to an admin user. If True, scopes should be an empty array.|
|» scopes|body|[string]|true|Provide list of scopes that should be given to teammate. If specifying list of scopes, is_admin should be set to False.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "address": "123 Acme St",
  "address2": "",
  "city": "City",
  "company": "ACME Inc.",
  "country": "USA",
  "email": "teammate1@example.com",
  "first_name": "Jane",
  "is_admin": false,
  "last_name": "Doe",
  "phone": "123-345-3453",
  "scopes": [
    "user.profile.read",
    "user.profile.edit"
  ],
  "state": "CA",
  "user_type": "teammate",
  "username": "teammate1",
  "website": "www.example.com",
  "zip": "12345"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "scopes",
      "message": "one or more of given scopes are invalid"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "username",
      "message": "username not found"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-teammates-permissions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request||Inline|
|404|Not Found||Inline|

<h3 id="update-teammates-permissions-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|

|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|sender_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the sender identity that you want to retrieve.|
|body|body|[sender-id-request](#schemasender-id-request)|false|none|
|» address|body|string|false|The physical address of the sender identity.|
|» address_2|body|string|false|Additional sender identity address information.|
|» city|body|string|false|The city of the sender identity.|
|» country|body|string|false|The country of the sender identity.|
|» from|body|object|false|none|
|» » email|body|string|false|The email address from which your recipient will receive emails.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name appended to the from email field. Typically your name or company name.|
|» nickname|body|string|false|A nickname for the sender identity. Not used for sending.|
|» reply_to|body|object|false|none|
|» » email|body|string|false|The email address to which your recipient will reply.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name appended to the reply to email field. Typically your name or company name.|
|» state|body|string|false|The state of the sender identity.|
|» zip|body|string|false|The zipcode of the sender identity.|

## Create an SSO Integration

<a id="opIdPOST_sso-integrations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sso/integrations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "completed_integration": true,
    "enabled": true,
    "entity_id": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "signin_url": "string",
    "signout_url": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /sso/integrations`

**This endpoint allows you to create an SSO integration.**

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "completed_integration": true,
  "enabled": true,
  "entity_id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "signin_url": "string",
  "signout_url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-sso-integration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[create-integration-request](#schemacreate-integration-request)|false|none|
|» completed_integration|body|boolean|false|Indicates if the integration is complete.|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|Indicates if the integration is enabled.|
|» entity_id|body|string|true|An identifier provided by your IdP to identify Twilio SendGrid in the SAML interaction. This is called the "SAML Issuer ID" in the Twilio SendGrid UI.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of your integration. This name can be anything that makes sense for your organization (eg. Twilio SendGrid)|
|» signin_url|body|string|true|The IdP's SAML POST endpoint. This endpoint should receive requests and initiate an SSO login flow. This is called the "Embed Link" in the Twilio SendGrid UI.|

The email provided for this user will also function as the Teammate’s username.

## Edit an SSO Teammate

<a id="opIdPATCH_sso-teammates-username"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sso/teammates/user%40example.com \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "email": "jane_doe@example.com",
    "first_name": "Jane",
    "is_admin": false,
    "last_name": "Doe",
    "scopes": [
      "mail.batch.create",
      "mail.batch.delete",
      "mail.batch.read",
      "mail.batch.update",
      "mail.send"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /sso/teammates/{username}`

**This endpoint allows you to modify an existing SSO Teammate.**

To turn a teammate into an admin, the request body should contain the `is_admin` field set to `true`. Otherwise, set `is_admin` to false and pass in all the scopes that a teammate should have.

Only the parent user and Teammates with admin permissions can update another Teammate’s permissions. Admin users can only update permissions.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "jane_doe@example.com",
  "first_name": "Jane",
  "is_admin": false,
  "last_name": "Doe",
  "scopes": [
    "mail.batch.create",
    "mail.batch.delete",
    "mail.batch.read",
    "mail.batch.update",
    "mail.send"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="edit-an-sso-teammate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|path|string(email)|true|This email address must be the same address assigned to the teammate in your IdP|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» first_name|body|string|false|none|
|» is_admin|body|boolean|false|none|
|» last_name|body|string|false|none|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|none|

## Retrieve Subuser Reputations

<a id="opIdGET_subusers-reputations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/subusers/reputations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /subusers/reputations`

**This endpoint allows you to request the reputations for your subusers.**

Subuser sender reputations give a good idea how well a sender is doing with regards to how recipients and recipient servers react to the mail that is being received. When a bounce, spam report, or other negative action happens on a sent email, it will affect your sender rating.

<h3 id="retrieve-subuser-reputations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

## Update IPs assigned to a subuser

<a id="opIdPUT_subusers-subuser_name-ips"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/subusers/string/ips \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '[
    "127.0.0.1"
  ]'
```

`PUT /subusers/{subuser_name}/ips`

**This endpoint allows you update your subusers' assigned IP.**

Each subuser should be assigned to an IP address from which all of this subuser's mail will be sent. Often, this is the same IP as the parent account, but each subuser can have one or more of their own IP addresses as well. 

More information:

* [How to request more IPs](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/dedicated-ip-addresses/)
* [Setup Reverse DNS](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/how-to-set-up-reverse-dns/)

> Body parameter

```json
[
  "127.0.0.1"
]
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subuser_name|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[string(ipv4)]|false|none|

```json
{
  "ips": [
    "127.0.0.1"
  ]
}
```

```json
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-subuser-statistics">Subuser Statistics</h1>

## Retrieve email statistics for your subusers.

<a id="opIdGET_subusers-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/subusers/stats?subusers=string&start_date=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /subusers/stats`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve the email statistics for the given subusers.**

You may retrieve statistics for up to 10 different subusers by including an additional _subusers_ parameter for each additional subuser.

<h3 id="retrieve-email-statistics-for-your-subusers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of results returned per page.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The point in the list to begin retrieving results from.|
|aggregated_by|query|string|false|How to group the statistics. Must be either "day", "week", or "month".|
|subusers|query|string|true|The subuser you want to retrieve statistics for. You may include this parameter up to 10 times to retrieve statistics for multiple subusers.|
|start_date|query|string|true|The starting date of the statistics to retrieve. Must follow format YYYY-MM-DD.|
|end_date|query|string|false|The end date of the statistics to retrieve. Defaults to today.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|aggregated_by|day|
|aggregated_by|week|
|aggregated_by|month|

## Retrieve monthly stats for all subusers

<a id="opIdGET_subusers-stats-monthly"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/subusers/stats/monthly?date=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /subusers/stats/monthly`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve the monthly email statistics for all subusers over the given date range.**

When using the `sort_by_metric` to sort your stats by a specific metric, you can not sort by the following metrics:
`bounce_drops`, `deferred`, `invalid_emails`, `processed`, `spam_report_drops`, `spam_reports`, or `unsubscribe_drops`.

<h3 id="retrieve-monthly-stats-for-all-subusers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|date|query|string|true|The date of the month to retrieve statistics for. Must be formatted YYYY-MM-DD|
|subuser|query|string|false|A substring search of your subusers.|
|sort_by_metric|query|string|false|The metric that you want to sort by. Metrics that you can sort by are: `blocks`, `bounces`, `clicks`, `delivered`, `opens`, `requests`, `unique_clicks`, `unique_opens`, and `unsubscribes`.'|
|sort_by_direction|query|string|false|The direction you want to sort.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Optional field to limit the number of results returned.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Optional beginning point in the list to retrieve from.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_by_metric|blocks|
|sort_by_metric|bounces|
|sort_by_metric|clicks|
|sort_by_metric|delivered|
|sort_by_metric|opens|
|sort_by_metric|requests|
|sort_by_metric|unique_clicks|
|sort_by_metric|unique_opens|
|sort_by_metric|unsubscribes|
|sort_by_direction|desc|
|sort_by_direction|asc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "stats": [
    {
```

## Delete blocks

<a id="opIdDELETE_suppression-blocks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/suppression/blocks \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "delete_all": false,
    "emails": [
      "example1@example.com",
      "example2@example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /suppression/blocks`

**This endpoint allows you to delete all email addresses on your blocks list.**

There are two options for deleting blocked emails: 

1. You can delete all blocked emails by setting `delete_all` to `true` in the request body. 
2. You can delete a selection of blocked emails by specifying the email addresses in the `emails` array of the request body.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "delete_all": false,
  "emails": [
    "example1@example.com",
    "example2@example.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="delete-blocks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» delete_all|body|boolean|false|Indicates if you want to delete all blocked email addresses.|
|» emails|body|[string]|false|The specific blocked email addresses that you want to delete.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="delete-blocks-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||Inline|

Authorization

## Delete spam reports

<a id="opIdDELETE_suppression-spam_reports"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/suppression/spam_reports \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "delete_all": false,
    "emails": [
      "example1@example.com",
      "example2@example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /suppression/spam_reports`

**This endpoint allows you to delete your spam reports.**

Deleting a spam report will remove the suppression, meaning email will once again be sent to the previously suppressed address. This should be avoided unless a recipient indicates they wish to receive email from you again. You can use our [bypass filters](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/sending-email/index-suppressions/#bypass-suppressions) to deliver messages to otherwise suppressed addresses when exceptions are required.

There are two options for deleting spam reports: 

1. You can delete all spam reports by setting the `delete_all` field to `true` in the request body.
2. You can delete a list of select spam reports by specifying the email addresses in the `emails` array of the request body.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "delete_all": false,
  "emails": [
    "example1@example.com",
    "example2@example.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="delete-spam-reports-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» delete_all|body|boolean|false|Indicates if you want to delete all email addresses on the spam report list.|
|» emails|body|[string]|false|A list of specific email addresses that you want to remove from the spam report list.|

> Example responses

> 204 Response

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="delete-spam-reports-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||Inline|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization
</aside>

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-transactional-templates-versions">Transactional Templates Versions</h1>

## Create a new transactional template version.

<a id="opIdPOST_templates-template_id-versions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/templates/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/versions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "active": 1,
    "editor": "design",
    "generate_plain_content": false,
    "html_content": "dolor",
    "name": "pariatur non incididunt commodo",
    "plain_content": "labore dolore",
    "subject": "aliquip nulla Ut",
    "template_id": "Excepteur Ut qui"
  }'
```

`POST /templates/{template_id}/versions`

**This endpoint allows you to create a new version of a template.**

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "active": 1,
  "editor": "design",
  "generate_plain_content": false,
  "html_content": "dolor",
  "name": "pariatur non incididunt commodo",
  "plain_content": "labore dolore",
  "subject": "aliquip nulla Ut",
  "template_id": "Excepteur Ut qui"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-transactional-template-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|template_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[transactional_template_version_create](#schematransactional_template_version_create)|false|none|
|» active|body|integer|false|Set the version as the active version associated with the template (0 is inactive, 1 is active). Only one version of a template can be active. The first version created for a template will automatically be set to Active.|
|» editor|body|string|false|The editor used in the UI.|
|» generate_plain_content|body|boolean|false|If true, plain_content is always generated from html_content. If false, plain_content is not altered.|
|» html_content|body|string|false|The HTML content of the version. Maximum of 1048576 bytes allowed.|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the transactional template version.|
|» plain_content|body|string|false|Text/plain content of the transactional template version. Maximum of 1048576 bytes allowed.|
|» subject|body|string|true|Subject of the new transactional template version.|
|» test_data|body|string|false|For dynamic templates only, the mock json data that will be used for template preview and test sends.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» active|0|
|» active|1|
|» editor|code|
|» editor|design|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "active": 1,
  "editor": "code",
  "generate_plain_content": true,
  "html_content": "<%body%>",
  "id": "8aefe0ee-f12b-4575-b5b7-c97e21cb36f3",
  "name": "example_version_name",
  "plain_content": "<%body%>",
  "subject": "<%subject%>",
  "template_id": "ddb96bbc-9b92-425e-8979-99464621b543",
  "updated_at": "2019-03-13 18:56:33"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-transactional-template-version-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||[transactional_template_version_output](#schematransactional_template_version_output)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization
</aside>

## Retrieve Click Track Settings

<a id="opIdGET_tracking_settings-click"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /tracking_settings/click`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve your current click tracking setting.**

Click Tracking overrides all the links and URLs in your emails and points them to either SendGrid’s servers or the domain with which you branded your link. When a customer clicks a link, SendGrid tracks those [clicks](https://sendgrid.com/docs/glossary/clicks/).

Click tracking helps you understand how users are engaging with your communications. SendGrid can track up to 1000 links per email

<h3 id="retrieve-click-track-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

```json
  "enabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-click-track-settings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||[click-tracking](#schemaclick-tracking)|

<aside class="warning">

Authorization
</aside>

## Get Open Tracking Settings

<a id="opIdGET_tracking_settings-open"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/tracking_settings/open \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /tracking_settings/open`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve your current settings for open tracking.**

Open Tracking adds an invisible image at the end of the email which can track email opens.

If the email recipient has images enabled on their email client, a request to SendGrid’s server for the invisible image is executed and an open event is logged.

These events are logged in the Statistics portal, Email Activity interface, and are reported by the Event Webhook.

<h3 id="get-open-tracking-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "enabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="get-open-tracking-settings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="get-open-tracking-settings-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicates if open tracking is enabled.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization
</aside>

## Retrieve current Enforced TLS settings.

<a id="opIdGET_user-settings-enforced_tls"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/settings/enforced_tls \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /user/settings/enforced_tls`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve your current Enforced TLS settings.**

The Enforced TLS settings specify whether or not the recipient is required to support TLS or have a valid certificate.

If either `require_tls` or `require_valid_cert` is set to `true`, the recipient must support TLS 1.1 or higher or have a valid certificate. If these conditions are not met, Twilio SendGrid will drop the message and send a block event with “TLS required but not supported” as the description.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

```json

  "require_tls": false,
  "require_valid_cert": false
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",

    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "errors": [

    }
  ]
}
```

```json
    {

    }
  ]
}
```

## Update Enforced TLS settings

<a id="opIdPATCH_user-settings-enforced_tls"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/settings/enforced_tls \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \

    "require_tls": true,
    "require_valid_cert": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /user/settings/enforced_tls`

**This endpoint allows you to update your Enforced TLS settings.**

To require TLS from recipients, set `require_tls` to `true`. If either `require_tls` or `require_valid_cert` is set to `true`, the recipient must support TLS 1.1 or higher or have a valid certificate. If these conditions are not met, Twilio SendGrid will drop the message and send a block event with “TLS required but not supported” as the description.

> Twilio SendGrid supports TLS 1.1 and higher and does not support older versions of TLS due to security vulnerabilities.

> Body parameter

```json
  "require_tls": true,
  "require_valid_cert": true
}
```

|» require_tls|body|boolean|false|Indicates if you want to require your recipients to support TLS. |
|» require_valid_cert|body|boolean|false|Indicates if you want to require your recipients to have a valid certificate.|

`GET /user/webhooks/event/settings`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve your current event webhook settings.**

If an event type is marked as `true`, then the event webhook will include information about that event.

SendGrid’s Event Webhook will notify a URL of your choice via HTTP POST with information about events that occur as SendGrid processes your email.

Common uses of this data are to remove unsubscribes, react to spam reports, determine unengaged recipients, identify bounced email addresses, or create advanced analytics of your email program.

```json
  "deferred": false,
  "delivered": false,
  "dropped": true,

  "group_resubscribe": false,
  "group_unsubscribe": false,
  "oauth_client_id": "est fugiat",

  "open": true,
  "processed": false,

  "unsubscribe": true,

}
```

```bash
  }'
```

`PATCH /user/webhooks/event/settings`

**This endpoint allows you to update your current event webhook settings.**

If an event type is marked as `true`, then the event webhook will include information about that event.

SendGrid’s Event Webhook will notify a URL of your choice via HTTP POST with information about events that occur as SendGrid processes your email.

Common uses of this data are to remove unsubscribes, react to spam reports, determine unengaged recipients, identify bounced email addresses, or create advanced analytics of your email program.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bounce": true,
  "click": true,
  "deferred": true,
  "delivered": true,
  "dropped": true,
  "enabled": true,
  "group_resubscribe": true,
  "group_unsubscribe": true,
  "oauth_client_id": "string",
  "oauth_client_secret": "string",
  "oauth_token_url": "string",
  "open": true,
  "processed": true,
  "spam_report": true,
  "unsubscribe": true,
  "url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-event-notification-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[event-webhook-update-oauth-request](#schemaevent-webhook-update-oauth-request)|false|none|
|» bounce|body|boolean|true|Receiving server could not or would not accept message.|
|» click|body|boolean|true|Recipient clicked on a link within the message. You need to enable Click Tracking for getting this type of event.|
|» deferred|body|boolean|true|Recipient's email server temporarily rejected message.|
|» delivered|body|boolean|true|Message has been successfully delivered to the receiving server.|
|» dropped|body|boolean|true|You may see the following drop reasons: Invalid SMTPAPI header, Spam Content (if spam checker app enabled), Unsubscribed Address, Bounced Address, Spam Reporting Address, Invalid, Recipient List over Package Quota|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|Indicates if the event webhook is enabled.|
|» group_resubscribe|body|boolean|true|Recipient resubscribes to specific group by updating preferences. You need to enable Subscription Tracking for getting this type of event.|
|» group_unsubscribe|body|boolean|true|Recipient unsubscribe from specific group, by either direct link or updating preferences. You need to enable Subscription Tracking for getting this type of event.|
|» oauth_client_id|body|string|false|The client ID Twilio SendGrid sends to your OAuth server or service provider to generate an OAuth access token. When passing data in this field, you must also include the oauth_token_url field.|
|» oauth_client_secret|body|string|false|This secret is needed only once to create an access token. SendGrid will store this secret, allowing you to update your Client ID and Token URL without passing the secret to SendGrid again.  When passing data in this field, you must also include the oauth_client_id and oauth_token_url fields.|
|» oauth_token_url|body|string|false|The URL where Twilio SendGrid sends the Client ID and Client Secret to generate an access token. This should be your OAuth server or service provider. When passing data in this field, you must also include the oauth_client_id field.|
|» open|body|boolean|true|Recipient has opened the HTML message. You need to enable Open Tracking for getting this type of event.|
|» processed|body|boolean|true|Message has been received and is ready to be delivered.|
|» spam_report|body|boolean|true|Recipient marked a message as spam.|
|» unsubscribe|body|boolean|true|Recipient clicked on message's subscription management link. You need to enable Subscription Tracking for getting this type of event.|
|» url|body|string|true|The URL that you want the event webhook to POST to.|

```json
{
  "bounce": true,
  "click": false,
  "deferred": true,
  "delivered": true,
  "dropped": true,
  "enabled": true,
  "group_resubscribe": false,
  "group_unsubscribe": true,
  "oauth_client_id": "anim sunt",
```

## Test Event Notification Settings

<a id="opIdPOST_user-webhooks-event-test"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/webhooks/event/test \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "oauth_client_id": "nisi",
    "oauth_client_secret": "veniam commodo ex sunt",
    "oauth_token_url": "dolor Duis",
    "url": "mollit non ipsum magna"
  }'
```

`POST /user/webhooks/event/test`

**This endpoint allows you to test your event webhook by sending a fake event notification post to the provided URL.**

SendGrid’s Event Webhook will notify a URL of your choice via HTTP POST with information about events that occur as SendGrid processes your email.

Common uses of this data are to remove unsubscribes, react to spam reports, determine unengaged recipients, identify bounced email addresses, or create advanced analytics of your email program.

>**Tip**: Retry logic for this endpoint differs from other endpoints, which use a rolling 24-hour retry.

If your web server does not return a 2xx response type, we will retry a POST request until we receive a 2xx response or the maximum time of 10 minutes has expired.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "oauth_client_id": "nisi",
  "oauth_client_secret": "veniam commodo ex sunt",
  "oauth_token_url": "dolor Duis",
  "url": "mollit non ipsum magna"
}
```

<h3 id="test-event-notification-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» oauth_client_id|body|string|false|The client ID Twilio SendGrid sends to your OAuth server or service provider to generate an OAuth access token. When passing data in this field, you must also include the oauth_client_secret and oauth_token_url fields.|
|» oauth_client_secret|body|string|false|This secret is needed only once to create an access token. SendGrid will store this secret, allowing you to update your Client ID and Token URL without passing the secret to SendGrid again.  When passing data in this field, you must also include the oauth_client_id and oauth_token_url fields.|
|» oauth_token_url|body|string|false|The URL where Twilio SendGrid sends the Client ID and Client Secret to generate an access token. This should be your OAuth server or service provider.  When passing data in this field, you must also include the oauth_client_id and oauth_client_secret fields.|
|» url|body|string|false|The URL where you would like the test notification to be sent.|

<h3 id="test-event-notification-settings-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||None|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization

## Retrieves Inbound Parse Webhook statistics.

<a id="opIdGET_user-webhooks-parse-stats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/user/webhooks/parse/stats?start_date=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /user/webhooks/parse/stats`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve the statistics for your Parse Webhook useage.**

SendGrid's Inbound Parse Webhook allows you to parse the contents and attachments of incomming emails. The Parse API can then POST the parsed emails to a URL that you specify. The Inbound Parse Webhook cannot parse messages greater than 30MB in size, including all attachments.

There are a number of pre-made integrations for the SendGrid Parse Webhook which make processing events easy. You can find these integrations in the [Library Index](https://sendgrid.com/docs/Integrate/libraries.html#-Webhook-Libraries).

<h3 id="retrieves-inbound-parse-webhook-statistics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|string|false|The number of statistics to return on each page.|
|offset|query|string|false|The number of statistics to skip.|
|aggregated_by|query|string|false|How you would like the statistics to by grouped. |
|start_date|query|string|true|The starting date of the statistics you want to retrieve. Must be in the format YYYY-MM-DD|
|end_date|query|string|false|The end date of the statistics you want to retrieve. Must be in the format YYYY-MM-DD|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|aggregated_by|day|
|aggregated_by|week|
|aggregated_by|month|

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-settings---inbound-parse">Settings - Inbound Parse</h1>

## Create a parse setting

<a id="opIdPOST_user-webhooks-parse-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/webhooks/parse/settings \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "hostname": "myhostname.com",
    "send_raw": true,
    "spam_check": false,
    "url": "http://email.myhostname.com"
  }'
```

`POST /user/webhooks/parse/settings`

**This endpoint allows you to create a new inbound parse setting.**

Creating an Inbound Parse setting requires two pieces of information: a `url` and a `hostname`.

The `hostname` must correspond to a domain authenticated by Twilio SendGrid on your account. If you need to complete domain authentication, you can use the [Twilio SendGrid App](https://app.sendgrid.com/settings/sender_auth) or the "Authenticate a domain" endpoint. See "[How to Set Up Domain Authentication](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/how-to-set-up-domain-authentication/)" for instructions.

Any email received by the `hostname` will be parsed when you complete this setup. You must also add a Twilio SendGrid MX record to this domain's DNS records. See "[Setting up the Inbound Parse Webhook](https://sendgrid.com/docs/for-developers/parsing-email/setting-up-the-inbound-parse-webhook/)" for full instructions.

The `url` represents a location where the parsed message data will be delivered. Twilio SendGrid will make an HTTP POST request to this `url` with the message data. The `url` must be publicly reachable, and your application must return a `200` status code to signal that the message data has been received.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "hostname": "myhostname.com",
  "send_raw": true,
  "spam_check": false,
  "url": "http://email.myhostname.com"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-parse-setting-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[parse-setting](#schemaparse-setting)|false|none|
|» hostname|body|string|false|A specific and unique domain or subdomain that you have created to use exclusively to parse your incoming email. For example, `parse.yourdomain.com`.|
|» send_raw|body|boolean|false|Indicates if you would like SendGrid to post the original MIME-type content of your parsed email. When this parameter is set to `true`, SendGrid will send a JSON payload of the content of your email.|
|» spam_check|body|boolean|false|Indicates if you would like SendGrid to check the content parsed from your emails for spam before POSTing them to your domain.|
|» url|body|string|false|The public URL where you would like SendGrid to POST the data parsed from your email. Any emails sent with the given hostname provided (whose MX records have been updated to point to SendGrid) will be parsed and POSTed to this URL.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "hostname": "myhostname.com",
  "send_raw": true,
  "spam_check": false,
  "url": "http://email.myhostname.com"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "field_name",
      "message": "error message"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|» hostname|body|string|false|A specific and unique domain or subdomain that you have created to use exclusively to parse your incoming email. For example, `parse.yourdomain.com`.|
|» send_raw|body|boolean|false|Indicates if you would like SendGrid to post the original MIME-type content of your parsed email. When this parameter is set to `true`, SendGrid will send a JSON payload of the content of your email.|
|» spam_check|body|boolean|false|Indicates if you would like SendGrid to check the content parsed from your emails for spam before POSTing them to your domain.|
|» url|body|string|false|The public URL where you would like SendGrid to POST the data parsed from your email. Any emails sent with the given hostname provided (whose MX records have been updated to point to SendGrid) will be parsed and POSTed to this URL.|

|» » » has_known_bounces|boolean|true|none|WHether email sent to this address from your account has bounced.|

|» » local_part|object|true|none|Checks on the local part of the email address.|

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-sender-verification">Sender Verification</h1>

## Get All Verified Senders

<a id="opIdGET_verified_senders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/verified_senders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /verified_senders`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve all the Sender Identities associated with an account.**

This endpoint will return both verified and unverified senders.

You can limit the number of results returned using the `limit`, `lastSeenID`, and `id` query string parameters.

* `limit` allows you to specify an exact number of Sender Identities to return.
* `lastSeenID` will return senders with an ID number occuring after the passed in ID. In other words, the `lastSeenID` provides a starting point from which SendGrid will iterate to find Sender Identities associated with your account.
* `id` will return information about only the Sender Identity passed in the request.

<h3 id="get-all-verified-senders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|number|false|none|
|lastSeenID|query|number|false|none|
|id|query|integer|false|none|

## Create Verified Sender Request

<a id="opIdPOST_verified_senders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/verified_senders \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "1234 Fake St",
    "address2": "PO Box 1234",
    "city": "San Francisco",
    "country": "USA",
    "from_email": "orders@example.com",
    "from_name": "Example Orders",
    "nickname": "Orders",
    "reply_to": "orders@example.com",
    "reply_to_name": "Example Orders",
    "state": "CA",
    "zip": "94105"
  }'
```

`POST /verified_senders`

**This endpoint allows you to create a new Sender Identify**.

Upon successful submission of a `POST` request to this endpoint, an identity will be created, and a verification email will be sent to the address assigned to the `from_email` field. You must complete the verification process using the sent email to fully verify the sender.

If you need to resend the verification email, you can do so with the Resend Verified Sender Request, `/resend/{id}`, endpoint.

If you need to authenticate a domain rather than a Single Sender, see the [Domain Authentication API](https://sendgrid.api-docs.io/v3.0/domain-authentication/authenticate-a-domain).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "1234 Fake St",
  "address2": "PO Box 1234",
  "city": "San Francisco",
  "country": "USA",
  "from_email": "orders@example.com",
  "from_name": "Example Orders",
  "nickname": "Orders",
  "reply_to": "orders@example.com",
  "reply_to_name": "Example Orders",
  "state": "CA",
  "zip": "94105"
}
```

## Domain Warn List

<a id="opIdGET_verified_senders-domains"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/verified_senders/domains \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /verified_senders/domains`

**This endpoint returns a list of domains known to implement DMARC and categorizes them by failure type — hard failure or soft failure**.

Domains listed as hard failures will not deliver mail when used as a [Sender Identity](https://sendgrid.com/docs/for-developers/sending-email/sender-identity/) due to the domain's DMARC policy settings.

For example, using a `yahoo.com` email address as a Sender Identity will likely result in the rejection of your mail. For more information about DMARC, see [Everything about DMARC](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/sending-email/dmarc/).

```json
}
```

## Resend Verified Sender Request

<a id="opIdPOST_verified_senders-resend-id"></a>

```bash
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /verified_senders/resend/{id}`

**This endpoint allows you to resend a verification email to a specified Sender Identity**.

Passing the `id` assigned to a Sender Identity to this endpoint will resend a verification email to the `from_address` associated with the Sender Identity. This can be useful if someone loses their verification email or needs to have it resent for any other reason.

You can retrieve the IDs associated with Sender Identities by passing a "Get All Verified Senders" endpoint.

`GET /verified_senders/steps_completed`

**This endpoint allows you to determine which of SendGrid’s verification processes have been completed for an account**.

This endpoint returns boolean values, `true` and `false`, for [Domain Authentication](https://sendgrid.com/docs/for-developers/sending-email/sender-identity/#domain-authentication), `domain_verified`, and [Single Sender Verification](https://sendgrid.com/docs/for-developers/sending-email/sender-identity/#single-sender-verification), `sender_verified`, for the account.

An account may have one, both, or neither verification steps completed. If you need to authenticate a domain rather than a Single Sender, see the "Authenticate a domain" endpoint.

**This endpoint allows you to update an existing Sender Identity**.

<h1 id="email-activity-beta-email-cname-records">Email CNAME records</h1>

## Email DNS records to a co-worker

<a id="opIdPOST_whitelabel-dns-email"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/whitelabel/dns/email \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "domain_id": 46873408,
    "email": "my_colleague@example.com",
    "link_id": 29719392,
    "message": "DNS Record for verification"
  }'
```

`POST /whitelabel/dns/email`

**This endpoint is used to share DNS records with a colleagues**

Use this endpoint to send SendGrid-generated DNS record information to a co-worker so they can enter it into your DNS provider to validate your domain and link branding. 

What type of records are sent will depend on whether you have chosen Automated Security or not. When using Automated Security, SendGrid provides you with three CNAME records. If you turn Automated Security off, you are instead given TXT and MX records.

If you pass a `link_id` to this endpoint, the generated email will supply the DNS records necessary to complete [Link Branding](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/how-to-set-up-link-branding/) setup. If you pass a `domain_id` to this endpoint, the generated email will supply the DNS records needed to complete [Domain Authentication](https://sendgrid.com/docs/ui/account-and-settings/how-to-set-up-domain-authentication/). Passing both IDs will generate an email with the records needed to complete both setup steps.

You can retrieve all your domain IDs from the returned `id` fields for each domain using the "List all authenticated domains" endpoint. You can retrieve all of your link IDs using the "Retrieve all branded links" endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "domain_id": 46873408,
  "email": "my_colleague@example.com",
  "link_id": 29719392,
  "message": "DNS Record for verification"
}
```

<h3 id="email-dns-records-to-a-co-worker-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» domain_id|body|integer|true|The ID of your SendGrid domain record.|
|» email|body|string(email)|true|The email address to send the DNS information to.|
|» link_id|body|integer|true|none|
|» message|body|string|false|A custom text block to include in the email body sent with the records.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "errors": {
    "error": "string",
    "field": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="email-dns-records-to-a-co-worker-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||None|
|400|Bad Request||Inline|

<h3 id="email-dns-records-to-a-co-worker-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|object|false|none|none|
|» error|string|false|none|none|
|» field|string|false|none|none|

## Authenticate a domain

<a id="opIdPOST_whitelabel-domains"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/whitelabel/domains \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "automatic_security": false,
    "custom_spf": true,
    "default": true,
    "domain": "example.com",
    "ips": [
      "192.168.1.1",
      "192.168.1.2"
    ],
    "subdomain": "news",
    "username": "john@example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /whitelabel/domains`

**This endpoint allows you to authenticate a domain.**

If you are authenticating a domain for a subuser, you have two options:
1. Use the "username" parameter. This allows you to authenticate a domain on behalf of your subuser. This means the subuser is able to see and modify the authenticated domain.
2. Use the Association workflow (see Associate Domain section). This allows you to authenticate a domain created by the parent to a subuser. This means the subuser will default to the assigned domain, but will not be able to see or modify that authenticated domain. However, if the subuser authenticates their own domain it will overwrite the assigned domain.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "automatic_security": false,
  "custom_spf": true,
  "default": true,
  "domain": "example.com",
  "ips": [
    "192.168.1.1",
    "192.168.1.2"
  ],
  "subdomain": "news",
  "username": "john@example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="authenticate-a-domain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» automatic_security|body|boolean|false|Whether to allow SendGrid to manage your SPF records, DKIM keys, and DKIM key rotation.|
|» custom_dkim_selector|body|string|false|Add a custom DKIM selector. Accepts three letters or numbers.|
|» custom_spf|body|boolean|false|Specify whether to use a custom SPF or allow SendGrid to manage your SPF. This option is only available to authenticated domains set up for manual security.|
|» default|body|boolean|false|Whether to use this authenticated domain as the fallback if no authenticated domains match the sender's domain.|
|» domain|body|string|true|Domain being authenticated.|
|» ips|body|[string]|false|The IP addresses that will be included in the custom SPF record for this authenticated domain.|
|» subdomain|body|string|false|The subdomain to use for this authenticated domain.|
|» username|body|string|false|The username associated with this domain.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "automatic_security": true,
  "custom_spf": false,
  "default": true,
  "dns": {
    "dkim1": {
      "data": "s1.domainkey.u1446226.wl.sendgrid.net",
      "host": "s1._domainkey.example.com",
      "type": "cname",
      "valid": false
    },
    "dkim2": {
      "data": "s2.domainkey.u1446226.wl.sendgrid.net",
      "host": "s2._domainkey.example.com",
      "type": "cname",
      "valid": false
    },
    "mail_cname": {
      "data": "u1446226.wl.sendgrid.net",
      "host": "example.example.com",
      "type": "cname",
      "valid": false
    }
  },
  "domain": "example.com",
  "id": 302183,
  "ips": [],
  "legacy": false,
  "subdomain": "example",
  "user_id": 1446226,
  "username": "mbernier",
  "valid": false
}
```

## Get the default authentication

<a id="opIdGET_whitelabel-domains-default"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/whitelabel/domains/default \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /whitelabel/domains/default`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve the default authentication for a domain.**

When creating or updating a domain authentication, you can set the domain as a default. The default domain will be used to send all mail. If you have multiple authenticated domains, the authenticated domain matching the domain of the From address will be used, and the default will be overridden.

This endpoint will return a default domain and its details only if a default is set. You are not required to set a default. If you do not set a default domain, this endpoint will return general information about your domain authentication status.

## List the authenticated domain associated with the given user.

<a id="opIdGET_whitelabel-domains-subuser"></a>

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /whitelabel/domains/subuser`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve all of the authenticated domains that have been assigned to a specific subuser.**

Authenticated domains can be associated with (i.e. assigned to) subusers from a parent account. This functionality allows subusers to send mail using their parent's domain authentication. To associate an authenticated domain with a subuser, the parent account must first authenticate and validate the domain. The parent may then associate the authenticated domain via the subuser management tools.

<h3 id="list-the-authenticated-domain-associated-with-the-given-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|username|query|string|true|Username for the subuser to find associated authenticated domain.|

```json
{
  "automatic_security": false,
  "custom_spf": true,
  "default": false,
  "dns": {
    "dkim": {
      "data": "k=rsa; t=s; p=publicKey",
      "host": "s1._domainkey.example.com",
      "type": "txt",
      "valid": false
    },
    "domain_spf": {
      "data": "v=spf1 include:mail.example.com -all",
      "host": "example.com",
      "type": "txt",
      "valid": false
    },
    "mail_server": {
      "data": "sendgrid.net",
      "host": "mail.example.com",
      "type": "mx",
      "valid": false
    },
    "subdomain_spf": {
      "data": "v=spf1 ip4:192.168.1.1 ip4:192.168.0.1 -all",
      "host": "mail.example.com",
      "type": "txt",
      "valid": false
    }
  },
  "domain": "example.com",
  "id": 1,
  "ips": [],
  "legacy": false,
  "subdomain": "mail",
  "user_id": 7,
  "username": "mail@example.com",
  "valid": false
}
```

## Disassociate an authenticated domain from a given user.

<a id="opIdDELETE_whitelabel-domains-subuser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/whitelabel/domains/subuser \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`DELETE /whitelabel/domains/subuser`

**This endpoint allows you to disassociate a specific authenticated domain from a subuser.**

Authenticated domains can be associated with (i.e. assigned to) subusers from a parent account. This functionality allows subusers to send mail using their parent's domain authentication. <h1 id="email-activity-beta-reverse-dns">Reverse DNS</h1>

## Retrieve all reverse DNS records

<a id="opIdGET_whitelabel-ips"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/whitelabel/ips \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /whitelabel/ips`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve all of the Reverse DNS records created by this account.**

You may include a search key by using the `ip` query string parameter. This enables you to perform a prefix search for a given IP segment (e.g., `?ip="192."`).

Use the `limit` query string parameter to reduce the number of records returned. All records will be returned if you have fewer records than the specified limit.

The `offset` query string parameter allows you to specify a non-zero index from which records will be returned. For example, if you have ten records, `?offset=5` will return the last five records (at indexes 5 through 9). The list starts at index zero.

<h3 id="retrieve-all-reverse-dns-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of results to retrieve.|
|offset|query|integer|false|The point in the list of results to begin retrieving IP addresses from.|
|ip|query|string|false|The IP address segment that you'd like to use in a prefix search.|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "a_record": {
      "data": "192.168.1.1",
      "host": "o1.email.example.com",
      "type": "a",
      "valid": true
    },
    "domain": "example.com",
    "id": 1,
    "ip": "192.168.1.1",
    "legacy": false,
    "rdns": "o1.email.example.com",
    "subdomain": "email",
    "users": [
      {
        "user_id": 7,
        "username": "john@example.com"
      },
      {
        "user_id": 8,
        "username": "jane@example.com"
      }
    ],
    "valid": true
  },
  {
    "a_record": {
      "data": "192.168.1.2",
      "host": "o2.email.example.com",
      "type": "a",
      "valid": true
    },
    "domain": "example.com",
    "id": 2,
    "ip": "192.168.1.2",
    "legacy": false,
    "rdns": "o2.email.example.com",
    "subdomain": "email",
    "users": [
      {
        "user_id": 7,
        "username": "john@example.com"
      },
      {
        "user_id": 9,
        "username": "jane@example2.com"
      }
    ],
    "valid": true
  }
]
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

## Validate a reverse DNS record

<a id="opIdPOST_whitelabel-ips-id-validate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/whitelabel/ips/string/validate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /whitelabel/ips/{id}/validate`

**This endpoint allows you to validate a reverse DNS record.**

Always check the `valid` property of the response’s `validation_results.a_record` object. This field will indicate whether it was possible to validate the reverse DNS record. If the `validation_results.a_record.valid` is `false`, this indicates only that Twilio SendGrid could not determine the validity your reverse DNS record — it may still be valid.

If validity couldn’t be determined, you can check the value of `validation_results.a_record.reason` to find out why.

You can retrieve the IDs associated with all your reverse DNS records using the "Retrieve all reverse DNS records" endpoint.

<h3 id="validate-a-reverse-dns-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|id|path|string|true|The ID of the reverse DNS record that you would like to validate.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": 123456,
  "valid": false,
  "validation_results": {
    "a_record": {
      "reason": "Failed to resolve A Record at o1.ptr4283.example.com: lookup o1.ptr4283.example.com on 192.168.0.10:53: no such host",
      "valid": false
    }
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "Reverse DNS record not found."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "internal error getting rDNS"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="validate-a-reverse-dns-record-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|404|Not Found|Unexpected error in API call. See HTTP response body for details.|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error||Inline|

<h3 id="validate-a-reverse-dns-record-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer|true|none|The ID of the reverse DNS record.|
|valid|boolean|true|none|Indicates if the reverse DNS record is valid.|
|validation_results|object|true|none|The specific results of the validation.|
|» a_record|object|false|none|none|
|» » reason|string \| null|true|none|The reason the reverse DNS record could not be validated. Is `null` if the reverse DNS record was validated.|
|» » valid|boolean|true|none|Indicates if the reverse DNS record could be validated.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|valid|true|
|valid|false|
|» » valid|true|
|» » valid|false|

Status Code **404**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[object]|true|none|The error messages for the failed validation.|
|» message|string|true|none|A message describing why the reverse DNS could not be validated.|

Status Code **500**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[object]|true|none|The error messages for the failed validation.|
|» message|string|true|none|A message describing why the IP whitelabel could not be validated.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Authorization
</aside>

## Create a branded link

<a id="opIdPOST_whitelabel-links"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/whitelabel/links \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "default": true,
    "domain": "example.com",
    "subdomain": "mail"
  }'
```

`POST /whitelabel/links`

**This endpoint allows you to create a new branded link.**

To create the link branding, supply the root domain and, optionally, the subdomain — these go into separate fields in your request body. The root domain should match your FROM email address. If you provide a  subdomain, it must be different from the subdomain you used for authenticating your domain.

You can submit this request as one of your subusers if you include their ID in the `on-behalf-of` header in the request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "default": true,
  "domain": "example.com",
  "subdomain": "mail"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» default|body|boolean|false|Indicates if you want to use this link branding as the default or fallback. When setting a new default, the existing default link branding will have its default status removed automatically.|
|» domain|body|string|true|The root domain for the subdomain that you are creating the link branding for. This should match your FROM email address.|
|» subdomain|body|string|false|The subdomain to create the link branding for. Must be different from the subdomain you used for authenticating your domain.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|» default|true|
|» default|false|

```json
      "data": "sendgrid.net",
      "host": "mail.example.com",
      "type": "cname",
      "valid": true
    },
    "owner_cname": {
      "data": "sendgrid.net",
      "host": "7.example.com",
      "type": "cname",
      "valid": true

  "domain": "example.com",
  "id": 1,

}
```

## Retrieve the default branded link

<a id="opIdGET_whitelabel-links-default"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/whitelabel/links/default \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /whitelabel/links/default`

**This endpoint allows you to retrieve the default branded link.**

The default branded link is the actual URL to be used when sending messages. If you have more than one branded link, the default is determined by the following order:

* The validated branded link marked as `default` (set when you call the "Create a branded link" endpoint or by calling the "Update a branded link" endpoint on an existing link)
* Legacy branded links (migrated from the whitelabel wizard)
* Default SendGrid-branded links (i.e., `100.ct.sendgrid.net`)

You can submit this request as one of your subusers if you include their ID in the `on-behalf-of` header in the request.

<h3 id="retrieve-the-default-branded-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain|query|string|false|The domain to match against when finding the default branded link.|
|on-behalf-of|header|string|false|none|

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "default": false,
  "dns": {
    "domain_cname": {
      "data": "sendgrid.net",
      "host": "mail.example.com",
      "type": "cname",
      "valid": true
    },
    "owner_cname": {
      "data": "sendgrid.net",
      "host": "7.example.com",
      "type": "cname",
      "valid": true
    }
  },
  "domain": "example.com",
  "id": 1,
  "legacy": false,
  "subdomain": "mail",
  "user_id": 7,
  "username": "john@example.com",
  "valid": true
}
```

|group_unsubscribe|boolean|true|none|Recipient unsubscribe from specific group, by either direct link or updating preferences. You need to enable Subscription Tracking for getting this type of event.|

|oauth_token_url|string|false|none|The URL where Twilio SendGrid sends the Client ID and Client Secret to generate an access token. This should be your OAuth server or service provider.|
|open|boolean|true|none|Recipient has opened the HTML message. You need to enable Open Tracking for getting this type of event.|
|processed|boolean|true|none|Message has been received and is ready to be delivered.|
|spam_report|boolean|true|none|Recipient marked a message as spam.|
|unsubscribe|boolean|true|none|Recipient clicked on message's subscription management link. You need to enable Subscription Tracking for getting this type of event.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL that you want the event webhook to POST to.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|attempt_num|integer|false|none|Used with "deferred" events to indicate the attempt number out of 10. One "deferred" entry will exists under events array for each time a message was deferred with error message from the server. |
|bounce_type|string|true|none|Use to distinguish between types of bounces|
|event_name|string|true|none|Name of event|
|http_user_agent|string|true|none|Client recipient used to click or open message|
|mx_server|string|true|none|For example mx.gmail.com|
|processed|string|true|none|Date of when event occurred|
|reason|string|false|none|Explanation of what caused "bounced", "deferred", or "blocked". Usually contains error message from the server - e.g. message from gmail why mail was deferred|
|url|string|true|none|Used with "clicked" event to indicate which url the user clicked.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|bounce_type|bounced|
|bounce_type|blocked|
|bounce_type|expired|
|event_name|bounced|
|event_name|opened|
|event_name|clicked|
|event_name|processed|
|event_name|dropped|
|event_name|delivered|
|event_name|deferred|
|event_name|spam_report|
|event_name|unsubscribe|
|event_name|group_unsubscribe|
|event_name|group_resubscribe|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|from_email|string|true|none|none|
|msg_id|string|true|none|none|
|originating_ip|string(ipv4)|true|none|This is the IP of the user who sent the message.|
|outbound_ip|string(ipv4)|true|none|IP used to send to the remote MTA. Used by UI to display IP in detailed view|
|outbound_ip_type|string|true|none|Whether or not the outbound IP is dedicated vs shared|
|status|string|true|none|Quick summary of the status of a message|
|subject|string|true|none|none|
|teammate|string|true|none|Teammate's username|
|template_id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|to_email|string|true|none|none|
|unique_args|string|true|none|JSON hash of arbitrary key-value pairs|

<h2 id="tocS_parse-setting">parse-setting</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaparse-setting"></a>
<a id="schema_parse-setting"></a>
<a id="tocSparse-setting"></a>
<a id="tocsparse-setting"></a>

```json
{
  "hostname": "myhostname.com",
  "send_raw": true,
  "spam_check": false,
  "url": "http://email.myhostname.com"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|hostname|string|false|none|A specific and unique domain or subdomain that you have created to use exclusively to parse your incoming email. For example, `parse.yourdomain.com`.|
|send_raw|boolean|false|none|Indicates if you would like SendGrid to post the original MIME-type content of your parsed email. When this parameter is set to `true`, SendGrid will send a JSON payload of the content of your email.|
|spam_check|boolean|false|none|Indicates if you would like SendGrid to check the content parsed from your emails for spam before POSTing them to your domain.|
|url|string|false|none|The public URL where you would like SendGrid to POST the data parsed from your email. Any emails sent with the given hostname provided (whose MX records have been updated to point to SendGrid) will be parsed and POSTed to this URL.|

<a id="schema_reverse_dns"></a>
<a id="tocSreverse_dns"></a>
<a id="tocsreverse_dns"></a>

```json
{
  "a_record": {
    "data": "192.168.1.1",
    "host": "o1.email.example.com",
    "type": "a",
    "valid": true
  },
  "domain": "example.com",
  "id": 1,
  "ip": "192.168.1.1",
  "legacy": false,
  "rdns": "o1.email.example.com",
  "subdomain": "email",
  "users": [
    {
      "user_id": 7,
      "username": "john@example.com"
    },
    {
      "user_id": 8,
      "username": "jane@example.com"
    }
  ],
  "valid": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|a_record|object|true|none|none|
|domain|string|true|none|The root, or sending, domain.|
|id|integer|true|none|The ID of the Reverse DNS.|
|ip|string|true|none|The IP address that this Reverse DNS was created for.|
|last_validation_attempt_at|integer|false|none|A Unix epoch timestamp representing the last time of a validation attempt.|
|legacy|boolean|true|none|Indicates if this Reverse DNS was created using the legacy whitelabel tool. If it is a legacy whitelabel, it will still function, but you'll need to create a new Reverse DNS if you need to update it.|
|rdns|string|true|none|The reverse DNS record for the IP address. This points to the Reverse DNS subdomain.|
|subdomain|string|false|none|The subdomain created for this reverse DNS. This is where the rDNS record points.|
|users|[object]|true|none|The users who are able to send mail from the IP address.|
|valid|boolean|true|none|Indicates if this is a valid Reverse DNS.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|contacts_count|integer|true|none|Total number of contacts present in the segment|
|contacts_sample|[[contact_response](#schemacontact_response)]|true|none|A subset of all contacts that are in this segment|
|created_at|string|true|none|ISO8601 timestamp of when the object was created|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|ID assigned to the segment when created.|
|name|string|true|none|Name of the segment.|
|next_sample_update|string|true|none|ISO8601 timestamp of when the samples will be next updated|
|parent_list_ids|[string]|true|none|The array of list ids to filter contacts on when building this segment. It allows only one such list id for now. We will support more in future|
|query_dsl|string|true|none|SQL query which will filter contacts based on the conditions provided|
|query_version|string|true|none|If not set, segment contains a Query for use with Segment v1 APIs. If set to '2', segment contains a SQL query for use in v2.|
|sample_updated_at|string|true|none|ISO8601 timestamp of when the samples were last updated|
|status|[segment_status_response](#schemasegment_status_response)|true|none|Segment status indicates whether the segment's contacts will be updated periodically|
|updated_at|string|true|none|ISO8601 timestamp of when the object was last updated|

```json
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "name": "string",
  "next_sample_update": "string",
```

|id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|

|sample_updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|ISO8601 timestamp the sample was last updated|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|ISO8601 timestamp the object was last updated|

```json
{
```

```json
  "entity_id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "signin_url": "string",
  "signout_url": "string",

  "single_signon_url": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|completed_integration|boolean|false|none|Indicates if the integration is complete.|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicates if the integration is enabled.|
|entity_id|string|true|none|An identifier provided by your IdP to identify Twilio SendGrid in the SAML interaction. This is called the "SAML Issuer ID" in the Twilio SendGrid UI.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of your integration. This name can be anything that makes sense for your organization (eg. Twilio SendGrid)|
|signin_url|string|true|none|The IdP's SAML POST endpoint. This endpoint should receive requests and initiate an SSO login flow. This is called the "Embed Link" in the Twilio SendGrid UI.|
|signout_url|string|true|none|This URL is relevant only for an IdP-initiated authentication flow. If a user authenticates from their IdP, this URL will return them to their IdP when logging out.|
|audience_url|string|false|none|The URL where your IdP should POST its SAML response. This is the Twilio SendGrid URL that is responsible for receiving and parsing a SAML assertion. This is the same URL as the Single Sign-On URL when using SendGrid.|
|id|string|false|none|A unique ID assigned to the configuration by SendGrid.|
|last_updated|number|true|none|A timestamp representing the last time the configuration was modified.|
|single_signon_url|string|false|none|The URL where your IdP should POST its SAML response. This is the Twilio SendGrid URL that is responsible for receiving and parsing a SAML assertion. This is the same URL as the Audience URL when using SendGrid.|

|bounce_drops|integer|false|none|The number of emails that were dropped because of a bounce.|
|bounces|integer|false|none|The number of emails that bounced instead of being delivered.|
|deferred|integer|false|none|The number of emails that temporarily could not be delivered. |
|delivered|integer|false|none|The number of emails SendGrid was able to confirm were actually delivered to a recipient.|
|invalid_emails|integer|false|none|The number of recipients who had malformed email addresses or whose mail provider reported the address as invalid.|
|processed|integer|false|none|Requests from your website, application, or mail client via SMTP Relay or the API that SendGrid processed.|
|requests|integer|false|none|The number of emails that were requested to be delivered.|
|spam_report_drops|integer|false|none|The number of emails that were dropped due to a recipient previously marking your emails as spam.|
|spam_reports|integer|false|none|The number of recipients who marked your email as spam.|
|unsubscribe_drops|integer|false|none|The number of emails dropped due to a recipient unsubscribing from your emails.|
|unsubscribes|integer|false|none|The number of recipients who unsubscribed from your emails.|

<h2 id="tocS_webhooks-event-webhook-request">webhooks-event-webhook-request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawebhooks-event-webhook-request"></a>
<a id="schema_webhooks-event-webhook-request"></a>
<a id="tocSwebhooks-event-webhook-request"></a>
<a id="tocswebhooks-event-webhook-request"></a>

```json
{
  "bounce": true,
  "click": true,
  "deferred": true,
  "delivered": true,
  "dropped": true,
  "enabled": true,
  "group_resubscribe": true,
  "group_unsubscribe": true,
  "oauth_client_id": "string",
  "oauth_token_url": "string",
  "open": true,
  "processed": true,
  "spam_report": true,
  "unsubscribe": true,
  "url": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bounce|boolean|true|none|Receiving server could not or would not accept message.|
|click|boolean|true|none|Recipient clicked on a link within the message. You need to enable Click Tracking for getting this type of event.|
|deferred|boolean|true|none|Recipient's email server temporarily rejected message.|
|delivered|boolean|true|none|Message has been successfully delivered to the receiving server.|
|dropped|boolean|true|none|You may see the following drop reasons: Invalid SMTPAPI header, Spam Content (if spam checker app enabled), Unsubscribed Address, Bounced Address, Spam Reporting Address, Invalid, Recipient List over Package Quota|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Indicates if the event webhook is enabled.|
|group_resubscribe|boolean|true|none|Recipient resubscribes to specific group by updating preferences. You need to enable Subscription Tracking for getting this type of event.|
|group_unsubscribe|boolean|true|none|Recipient unsubscribe from specific group, by either direct link or updating preferences. You need to enable Subscription Tracking for getting this type of event.|
|oauth_client_id|string|false|none|The client ID Twilio SendGrid sends to your OAuth server or service provider to generate an OAuth access token. When passing data in this field, you must also include the oauth_token_url field.|
|oauth_token_url|string|false|none|The URL where Twilio SendGrid sends the Client ID and Client Secret to generate an access token. This should be your OAuth server or service provider. When passing data in this field, you must also include the oauth_client_id field.|
|open|boolean|true|none|Recipient has opened the HTML message. You need to enable Open Tracking for getting this type of event.|
|processed|boolean|true|none|Message has been received and is ready to be delivered.|
|spam_report|boolean|true|none|Recipient marked a message as spam.|
|unsubscribe|boolean|true|none|Recipient clicked on message's subscription management link. You need to enable Subscription Tracking for getting this type of event.|
|url|string|true|none|The URL that you want the event webhook to POST to.|
